## [403] ASSISTANT · 2026-10-18T18:16:24.017Z

That changes the interpretation of GrAnn significantly.

**GrAnn is the rotational synchronizer of the Whirligig.** Its primary job is not to generate extra spin from curvature, as I proposed earlier. It is to impose the smallest shared rotational cycle that closes the complete mechanism.

That means three things:

1. The sphere must complete its required rotations through **all three axes**, not merely spin around its rolling axis.
2. The R and Q curves must return to their starting configurations together, including their orientations and the moving crossbar.
3. The gimbal elbow must be rotationally locked to that common cycle, so its completed revolutions reflect the combined periodicities.

The curvature-to-spin experiment can remain a separate research branch, but it should not determine the main GrAnn locking rule.

## A simpler three-axis GrAnn construction

I tested a candidate that matches your functional description more closely.

Let \(g=(R+b)/b\) be the rolling ratio, and let \(N\) be the smallest admissible shared winding count. Choose the GrAnn radial-spin rate

\[
\sigma=\sqrt{N^2-g^2}.
\]

Then the sphere's angular velocity per unit torus-orbit angle is

\[
\boxed{
\frac{\boldsymbol\omega}{\dot\psi}
=
\sigma\cos\psi\,\hat{\mathbf x}
+\sigma\sin\psi\,\hat{\mathbf y}
-\frac{R}{b}\,\hat{\mathbf z}
}
\]

This uses **all three spatial axes** while preserving the selected-point rolling constraint at the torus wall.

For the existing default \(R=1.65,\ b=0.55\), the old ratio is \(g=4\). Choosing the smallest *even* \(N\) strictly greater than 4 gives **six GrAnn circuits per torus orbit**.

<grid columns={3} gap={2}>
  <grid-item>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">GrAnn circuits</text>
    <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>6</title>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Wall-contact residual</text>
    <title size="lg" color="default">~10⁻¹⁵</title>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Orientation closure residual</text>
    <title size="lg" color="default">~10⁻¹⁵</title>
  </grid-item>
</grid>

In the executed numerical test, X and Y both had nonzero rotational components, Z retained the required rolling component, and the sphere returned to its initial orientation.

This is a candidate **rotational-lock mechanism**, not yet a full R/Q implementation. It avoids requiring GrAnn's shape to generate an arbitrary extra rotation.

### The remaining arithmetic distinction

There are two related quantities we should keep separate:

\[
D=\operatorname{lcm}(q_x,q_y,q_z,q_R,q_Q)
\]

This gives the shortest return duration when the rotational rates are rational fractions \(p_i/q_i\) of a base circuit.

Then the number of completed turns in that duration is \(n_i=Dp_i/q_i\). Their least common multiple can supply the **elbow's gearing count**, if that is the mechanical rule you intend.

Those are not automatically the same number. And although all phases may return arithmetically, we still have to verify that the sphere's full orientation, both curve contacts, and the elbow actually return together.

I've saved the revised design and a separate Python prototype in HsH:

- [GrAnn minimum-return, three-axis locking specification](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-18.md)
- [GrAnn rotational-lock prototype](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/grann_rotational_lock.py)

The core three-axis construction was numerically tested, and both files were committed and read back. The new standalone CLI has not yet had its own execution check, and **the website has not yet been switched to this mechanism**.

One precise question before I wire the elbow: **When you say “common denominator,” do you want its number of revolutions to be the LCM of the individual completed rotation counts?** For example, if the required counts are 2, 3, and 4, the elbow would make 12 revolutions over their common cycle.

## [413] ASSISTANT · 2026-10-18T18:20:25.007Z

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
from math import sqrt, pi, lcm

def locked_grann(major=1.65, radius=.55, n=6, samples=1201):
    gear = (major + radius) / radius
    sigma = sqrt(n*n - gear*gear)
    psi = np.linspace(0, 2*pi, samples)
    er = np.column_stack((np.cos(psi), np.sin(psi), np.zeros_like(psi)))
    et = np.column_stack((-np.sin(psi), np.cos(psi), np.zeros_like(psi)))
    # World rotation: orbital Rz followed by a co-rotating GrAnn lock.
    Q = (
        Rotation.from_rotvec(np.column_stack((np.zeros_like(psi), np.zeros_like(psi), psi)))
        * Rotation.from_rotvec(np.outer(psi, np.array([sigma, 0., -gear])))
    ).as_matrix()
    bcontact = np.einsum("nji,nj->ni", Q, er)
    pivot = major*er + radius*np.einsum("nij,nj->ni", Q, bcontact)
    wall = (major+radius)*er
    omega = np.column_stack((sigma*er[:,0], sigma*er[:,1], -major/radius*np.ones_like(psi)))
    slip_analytic = major*et + np.cross(omega, radius*er)
    dQ = np.gradient(Q, psi, axis=0, edge_order=2)
    Omega = dQ@np.swapaxes(Q, 1, 2)
    w_fd = np.column_stack((Omega[:,2,1],Omega[:,0,2],Omega[:,1,0]))
    slip_fd = major*et + np.cross(w_fd, radius*er)
    body_path_length = np.sum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(bcontact,axis=0), axis=1))
    return dict(gear=gear,grann_turns=n,radial_spin=sigma,axis_omega_ranges={a:(float(omega[:,i].min()),float(omega[:,i].max())) for i,a in enumerate("xyz")},
                max_wall_error=float(np.linalg.norm(pivot-wall,axis=1).max()),
                max_slip=float(np.linalg.norm(slip_analytic,axis=1).max()),
                max_fd_slip=float(np.linalg.norm(slip_fd[5:-5],axis=1).max()),
                orientation_seam=float(np.linalg.norm(Q[0]-Q[-1])),
                measured_material_arclength=float(body_path_length),
                predicted_material_arclength=float(2*pi*gear),
                predicted_single_GrAnn_circuit_length=float(2*pi*gear/n))
for n in (4, 6, 8):
    print(n, locked_grann(n=n) if n>4 else "n=4 is degenerate: no x/y rotation")

## [433] ASSISTANT · 2026-10-21T12:19:20.947Z

The direction issue is real. In the old code, the selected contact was on the **outer radial wall** at \(R+b\), so its no-slip spin opposed the orbital motion. For your intended **inner wall** at \(R-b\), the contact offset reverses and the required rolling spin reverses with it:

\[
\omega_z=+\frac{R}{b}\dot\psi.
\]

I’m changing the contact itself, not just reversing the animation. The three-axis lock will preserve that inward-contact condition, with the elbow’s turn count derived from the common cycle rather than its own slider.

I’m fixing the integer boundary and rerunning the rotation and elbow-lock tests before saving it.

## [439] ASSISTANT · 2026-10-21T12:22:06.450Z

## Whirligig update: rolling corrected

The revised mechanical version is now committed to `Satobloc/HsH`.

**The ball now rolls against the inner torus wall**, with the required physical spin in the same direction as its orbital motion. This is a change to the contact geometry and rotation equations, not simply an animation reversal.

The default configuration now uses a minimum four-turn, three-axis GrAnn lock. The elbow's revolutions are computed from that lock and the R/Q sweep cycle rather than controlled by an independent slider.

The first executable checks passed:

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Inner-wall rolling slip residual | \(3.9\times10^{-16}\) |
| Full orientation return error | \(5.2\times10^{-15}\) |
| Elbow–torus intersections | 1,401 / 1,401 |
| Default GrAnn / elbow winding | 4 / 4 |
| Three R/Q sweeps | 12 locked elbow rotations |

The equal-diameter ball/tube contact is still a limiting geometric construction. These checks verify the nominated inner contact, not global no-slip over an extended contact region.

**[Updated Whirligig source](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html)**

## Comparator library expanded

The updated application now contains **42 equation profiles**: the original 14, plus 28 additional examples covering classical mechanics, field equations, statistical mechanics, special functions, potentials, solitons, and band geometry.

Two new discovery series are available:

- **Best-known series:** 11 familiar equations, including Kepler, Maxwell, Fourier heat flow, Schrödinger, and Planck.
- **Often overlooked series:** 17 less frequently demonstrated examples, including Jacobi theta, Bessel, Clausen, dilogarithms, Berry curvature, Mathieu, KdV, and sine–Gordon.

Instead of selecting pairs according to whether they produce appealing Curvy Lisa traces, the **Next pair** control walks through the series in deterministic order. The combined library offers **861 unique unordered pairs**, without aesthetic filtering.

The mathematical descriptions distinguish exact solutions from sampled observables, coefficient functions, approximate special-function evaluations, and periodic scans of otherwise nonperiodic solutions.

**[Expanded equation library in HsH](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html)**

## Saved and verified

The revised source, mathematical specification, equation library, and integration instructions have been saved to GitHub and independently read back.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html" title="Whirligig application"/> | Updated interactive mechanism and 42-equation selectors |
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_INNER_WALL_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-21.md" title="Updated GrAnn specification"/> | Inner-wall rolling derivation, three-axis locking, minimum return and elbow gearing |
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/grann_rotational_lock.py" title="Python rotational-lock prototype"/> | Updated inner-contact numerical model |
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/EQUATION_LIBRARY.md" title="Equation library documentation"/> | All comparator series, assumptions and sampling limitations |
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/SITES_INTEGRATION.md" title="Website integration instructions"/> | Builder handoff and live-site verification requirements |

The expanded JavaScript regression ran **84 configurations totaling 117,684 geometry samples**, with no missing torus-wall intersections, no east/west hemisphere violations, and perpendicularity and selected-contact residuals at floating-point precision.

An independent Python numerical check also confirmed positive inner-wall rolling spin, nonzero rotational components through all three axes, and full orientation closure. The standalone updated Python CLI itself has not yet been executed separately.

One distinction is preserved in the documentation: the older full Python R/Q engine still models an **outer-wall** contact branch. It has not been silently converted or represented as equivalent to this new implementation.

**Current status:** Saved in HsH and numerically checked. The original GrAnn self-intersection and full physical-contact behavior remain open research questions. Live Glass Sausage Factory deployment and graphical browser testing remain unverified.

Its selected contact obeys the analytic no-slip condition at one nominated point; because equal radii create a nonisolated contact set, this does <b>not</b> certify no-slip across every point of contact. There is no separate pen or projector. The only tracing member is the gimbal elbow, constrained perpendicular to the moving crossbar. GrAnn is a minimum-return three-axis rotational lock with the INNER torus selected contact at Donomphulon and opposite OUTER torus P_ivot; the radial construction is BigRad. The historical GrAnn_Omph self-intersection and GrAnn_t_ipode self-tangency remain unresolved. New rotational lock uses the INNER torus wall and drives the elbow from minimum even three-axis rotations via LCM. Two independently shaped source curves share a sweep clock; GrAnn's minimum rotational return sets the elbow-turn count by LCM, with no independently chosen curvature-gain phase. This is not a certified physical bearing model. No isomorphism or physical law is assumed. {"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_INNER_WALL_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-21.md","content":"# GrAnn / R\u2013Q Whirligig: inner-wall rolling and minimum shared rotational lock\n\n**Date:** 2026-10-21  \n**Status:** SANDBOXED browser engineering reconstruction, repository-published, real-browser/Sites deployment not independently verified.  \n**Source:** `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html` in `Satobloc/HsH`.  \n**User correction:** GrAnn is fundamentally rotational locking through **all three spatial axes**, with the **minimum shared return** determining the number of rotations of the single perpendicular gimbal elbow. The sphere rolls on the **inner radial surface of the torus**, not the outer one. The previously visible outward-contact spin looked backward because it was actually the wrong contact branch.\n\n## Selected contact and direction\n\nLet torus major radius be `R`, tube radius and sphere radius both `b=a`, orbital position `C(\u03c8)=R(cos\u03c8,sin\u03c8,0)=R e_r`, and orbit tangent `e_\u03c6`. The two torus radial equator points are:\n\n```text\nDonomphulon = P_inner = (R-b)e_r\nP_ivot      = P_outer = (R+b)e_r\nr_inner     = P_inner-C = -b e_r\nC'          = R e_\u03c6\n```\n\nNominated inner-wall no-slip requires `C' + \u03c9 \u00d7 (-b e_r) = 0` per unit `\u03c8`, hence the **z component** of angular velocity is `\u03c9_z=+R/b`, in the SAME physical sign as torus progression. For the old **outer** contact `r=+b e_r`, the required sign was `\u03c9_z=-R/b`. Reversing playback alone is not an acceptable fix: switch the selected wall, contact offset, and the resulting orientation/velocity constraint together.\n\nThe earlier browser version accidentally labeled its single inner contact as both P_ivot and Donomphulon. This is corrected: P_ivot remains the **outer** circumferential point per the historical source, while Donomphulon is the **inner** selected rolling point; the diameter `2b` separates them. The material GrAnn track passes through both contact and antipode.\n\n## Minimum even three-axis rotational lock\n\nWrite `r=R/b`, `\u03b4=r\u22121`. In this deliberately defined SO(3) locking ansatz, take\n\n```text\nn = smallest positive EVEN integer strictly larger than |\u03b4|\n\u03c3 = sqrt(n\u00b2\u2212\u03b4\u00b2)                              (nonzero transverse spin)\nu = (\u03c3,0,\u03b4)/n                               (unit body axis)\nQ(\u03c8) = Rot_z(\u03c8) Rot_u(n \u03c8)\n```\n\nThen the world angular velocity per `\u03c8` is\n\n```text\n\u03c9 = \u03c3 cos\u03c8 e_x + \u03c3 sin\u03c8 e_y + r e_z.\n```\n\nThe sphere therefore rotates through **x and y over the orbit** as well as the **positive z rolling direction**, without violating the nominated inner-wall slip constraint. Because `n` is an integer and the orbital angle makes a full turn, the complete orientation `Q(2\u03c0)=Q(0)`; the **smallest even** `n>|\u03b4|` makes the x/y component strictly nonzero. This is a minimality statement only **within this specified constant-oblique-axis ansatz**, not proof of a globally unique minimal mechanism.\n\nThe sphere's body material contact is\n\n```text\ng_body(\u03c8)=Q(\u03c8)\u207b\u00b9(\u2212e_r(\u03c8))\n```\n\nand the torus wall determines `C = P_inner - b Q g_body`. The resulting body track is a generally non-great circular GrAnn contact locus. Its historical self-intersection `GrAnn_Omph`, special antipodal self-tangency `GrAnn_t_ipode` and original R-anchor crossover **have not been reconstructed**. This lock is functional, not a claim to have recovered the exact source-described shape.\n\n## Crossbar and elbow timing\n\nR and Q remain independent E/W **sphere curves**. A common meridional sweep intersects both curves separately, yielding two moving body points `R(\u03c8)` and `Q(\u03c8)`. Their freely varying connector has midpoint W_obble; its one and only projecting gimbal elbow is constrained exactly perpendicular to the connector.\n\nThe current browser maps each selected input to one closed 2\u03c0 sphere curve, so one full normalized sweep lap returns both source curves to their represented starting parameters. Let `m` be the selectable **integer** number of complete sweeps per torus orbit. Define\n\n```text\nelbow_turns = lcm(n,m)\ntheta_elbow(\u03c8) = elbow_turns * \u03c8\n```\n\nThis replaces the former separate arbitrary elbow-turn slider and the ad hoc `curvature_gain*(curvature_R\u2212curvature_Q)` phase. The single gimbal elbow intersects the actual torus wall to make Curvy Lisa. The R/Q representation may have shorter scalar periods but a complete spatial curve still carries its azimuth winding; use full curve/orientation closure, not merely scalar equality, to test return.\n\nFor `R=1.65,b=.55`: `r=3,\u03b4=2,n=4,\u03c3=sqrt(12)`; default m=1 gives elbow=4, while m=3 gives elbow=12. Other radii choose their own minimal-even n with a floating-point guard at integer boundaries. General source-specific fractional windings, quaternion signs, nonperiodic solutions, nontrivial holonomy and independently varying follower phases would require a more general common-return solver; these are not silently presumed solved.\n\n## Unfiltered comparator series\n\nThe browser retains its original **14** equation adapters and adds **28** explicit scalar representatives. They are organized as:\n- **11 best-known examples:** harmonic oscillator, Kepler ellipse, Maxwell plane wave, Fourier heat equation, Laplace harmonic, Schr\u00f6dinger box eigenfunction, standing wave, Lorentz gamma scan, Planck spectrum, Maxwell\u2013Boltzmann speed distribution, Fermi\u2013Dirac occupation.\n- **17 often overlooked examples:** Jacobi theta, Legendre, Chebyshev, Bessel J0 (40-point quadrature), Clausen Cl2 (truncated), Re Li2 (truncated), Berry curvature in a two-band Dirac model, Mathieu coefficient, KdV one-soliton profile, sine\u2013Gordon kink, viscous Burgers shock, Morse and Lennard\u2013Jones potentials, Kitaev chain spectrum, P\u00f6schl\u2013Teller potential, Fresnel C (Simpson quadrature), U(1) Wilson phase.\n\nThese category labels are **editorial** and not an objective ranking of physical importance or novelty. Every profile remains selectable independently as R or Q, with a displayed formula, chosen representative and limitations. A deterministic no-ranking pair iterator traverses every unordered pair in the selected series: 55 best-known pairs, 136 overlooked pairs, or **861 combinations across all 42**. No automated beauty/tuning selection is applied to Curvy Lisa. Some source mathematical objects are nonperiodic; **the prescribed sample parameter is periodic**, not the original soliton, kink or trajectory.\n\n## Executed test record\n\nAll executed checks use the browser's JavaScript with a **stub DOM/canvas**, not a real graphical browser.\n- Default `R=1.65,b=.55,m=1`: `n=4,` `elbow_turns=4`, nonzero `\u03c3=3.4641`, inner contact slip residual under `3.9e\u221216`, full SO(3) orientation return residual under `5.3e\u221215`, 1,401/1,401 first-forward elbow/torus ray intersections.\n- `m=3` changes the locked elbow turns automatically to 12, with no independent elbow motor field.\n- All 42 profiles generated finite, matching samples at 0 and 2\u03c0. The unfiltered series controls advanced through the ordered pairs.\n- Full regression with all 42 profiles in the R selector and all 42 in the Q selector: **84 configurations, 117,684 evaluated apparatus samples**, zero missing torus wall hits or E/W violations, max bar/elbow unit-dot residual `4.45e\u221216`, max selected inner-contact slip residual `3.85e\u221216`.\n- The P_ivot (outer) / Donomphulon (inner) radial distance was tested as `2b=1.1` in the default reference.\n\n**Not verified:** actual published Sites page, real browser rendering/performance, dynamic no-slip at all points in the degenerate `a=b` full contact set, complete historical GrAnn topology, general equivalence of arbitrary physics equations, or a proof that Curvy Lisa equals a derivative.\n\n## Supersession\n\nThis replaces the earlier default **outer-wall** rolling sign, its great-circle-only GrAnn geometry, the formerly user-adjustable elbow turns/curvature-gain, and the old shortcut that identified the radius gear `(R+b)/b` as the complete GrAnn/R/Q common return. Those prior research files remain in the archive as historical records, not the current design.\n\nLive deployment requires the site builder to replace the existing `/laboratory/whirligig/` implementation from the current HsH source and verify the new inner contact, three-axis motion, unique outer and inner markers, automatic elbow count, and entire comparator series.\n","message":"Record corrected inner-torus rolling, three-axis GrAnn lock and unfiltered 42-equation pair series"}}

Then **D=12 torus circuits** and `(n_x,n_y,n_z,n_R,n_Q)=(6,4,3,12,2)`. Choose an integer `N>g` that satisfies the required even-parity and R/Q closure divisibility constraints, and choose the **smallest eligible** N. Set\n\n```\nsigma = sqrt(N^2-g^2) > 0\nK = (sigma, 0, -g)   ;  |K|=N\nQ(psi) = Rot_z(psi) * exp_SO3(psi [K]x)\n```\n\nwhere `[K]x` is the cross-product generator. With sphere center `C=R0 e_r` and contact offset `b e_r`:\n\n```\ndC/dpsi + (omega / psi_dot) cross (b e_r) = 0.\n```\n\nThe body-frame material contact locus is `G_body(psi)=Q(psi)^T e_r(psi)`. import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
from math import gcd, lcm, floor, pi, sqrt
def inner_audit(R=1.65,b=.55,sweep=1,nsteps=3001):
    delta=R/b-1
    n=2*(floor((abs(delta)+1e-10)/2)+1)
    sig=sqrt(n*n-delta*delta)
    psi=np.linspace(0,2*pi,nsteps)
    er=np.column_stack((np.cos(psi),np.sin(psi),np.zeros_like(psi)))
    et=np.column_stack((-np.sin(psi),np.cos(psi),np.zeros_like(psi)))
    orient=(Rotation.from_rotvec(psi[:,None]*np.array([0,0,1]))
            *Rotation.from_rotvec(psi[:,None]*np.array([sig,0,delta]))).as_matrix()
    gb=np.einsum('nji,nj->ni',orient,-er)
    c=R*er
    inner=c+b*np.einsum('nij,nj->ni',orient,gb)
    outer=c-b*np.einsum('nij,nj->ni',orient,gb)
    w=sig*er+(R/b)*np.array([0,0,1])
    slip=R*et+np.cross(w,-b*er)
    deriv=np.gradient(orient,psi,axis=0,edge_order=2)
    O=deriv@np.transpose(orient,(0,2,1))
    wf=np.column_stack((O[:,2,1],O[:,0,2],O[:,1,0]))
    slipfd=R*et+np.cross(wf,-b*er)
    return dict(major=R,b=b,min_turns=n,elbow=lcm(n,sweep),sigma=sig,
                inner_error=np.linalg.norm(inner-(R-b)*er,axis=1).max(),
                outer_error=np.linalg.norm(outer-(R+b)*er,axis=1).max(),
                selected_slip=np.linalg.norm(slip,axis=1).max(),
                fd_slip=np.linalg.norm(slipfd[5:-5],axis=1).max(),
                frame_seam=np.linalg.norm(orient[0]-orient[-1]),
                net_z_sign=np.min(w[:,2]),max_x=np.max(np.abs(w[:,0])),max_y=np.max(np.abs(w[:,1])))
[inner_audit(),inner_audit(sweep=3),inner_audit(R=1.6,b=.55),inner_audit(R=1.65,b=.55,nsteps=6001)]

This code does too.\n\n## Run\n\n```bash\npython -m pip install -r requirements.txt\npython whirligig.py --input example_equations.json --out output --search\npython plot_mechanics.py --input example_equations.json --out mechanics_snapshot.png --gif rolling_whirligig.gif\npython validate_mapping.py --input example_equations.json --out mapping_validation.json\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\n`--input` is optional: a two-harmonic-pair demonstration is built in.\n\n## Input equation adapters\n\nTwo independent specs are supplied as `R` and `Q` in a JSON file. Every adapter records its representation choice, physical units remain those of the caller, and original numerical coordinates are preserved apart from the sphere carrier. **No universal faithful parameterization exists for arbitrary symbolic equations without specifying a solution branch, observables, and a parameter interval.** Accordingly the tool supports:\n\n| Kind | Example | What is done | Limits |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `expression` | `0.5*cos(2*t)+0.1*sin(5*t)` | Scalar function encoded reversibly in sphere latitude; azimuth is `t` | Functions must be finite on the interval. Periodicity tested, not fabricated |\n| `parametric` | `{\"components\":[\"cos(t)\",\"sin(t)\"]}` | 2D trajectory via reversible stereographic embedding; 3D trajectory radialized with magnitude preserved separately | 3D radial projection loses magnitude in its sphere output |\n| `implicit` | `x*x/2.25+y*y-1=0` written as `x*x/2.25+y*y-1` | Extract largest closed real zero contour and stereographically lift | Grid approximate; must set bounding box and a suitable branch |\n| `ode` | `{\"rhs\":[\"y\",\"-x\"],\"initial\":[1,0]}` | Numerically integrates a 1\u20133 dimensional ODE and embeds the path | May not close; only specified initial-value solution is represented |\n| `sampled` | `{\"path\":\"path.csv\"}` | Arclength-resamples a closed 2D/3D numeric curve | Intended for PDE/GR/field equations solved upstream; refuses open CSV curves |\n\nExpression parsing is AST-restricted: arithmetic and common NumPy scalar mathematical functions only. No `eval()`, attribute access, user code import, or arbitrary shell expression execution.\n\nFor a PDE, differential geometry equation, non-Euclidean metric, or symbolic Schwarzschild geodesic, **first choose a solution and chart** and pass the resulting parametric/CSV path. This prevents smuggling an arbitrary metric into a falsely universal polar-projection routine. Keep the full source equation and domain as metadata outside the low-dimensional carrier.\n\n## Exact selected-contact rolling law\n\nLet the torus have major radius `R` and tube/minor radius `a`. Let the sphere have radius `b<a` and travel on a center circle of radius\n\n\\[\n\\rho=R+a-b,\\qquad C(\\psi)=\\rho(\\cos\\psi,\\sin\\psi,0).\n\\]\n\nThe selected contact on the outer equator is\n\n\\[\nP(\\psi)=(R+a)(\\cos\\psi,\\sin\\psi,0)=C+b\\mathbf e_r.\n\\]\n\nFor rolling without slip at this **isolated chosen point**, the laboratory angular velocity obeys\n\n\\[\n\\boldsymbol\\omega=-\\frac{\\rho}{b}\\dot\\psi\\mathbf e_z,\n\\quad \\dot C+\\boldsymbol\\omega\\times(b\\mathbf e_r)=0.\n\\]\n\nDefine the Great-Annulum body contact angle\n\n\\[\n\\gamma(\\psi)=\\frac{R+a}{b}\\psi.\n\\]\n\nLet `W(\u03c8)` be the orthonormal world frame `(e_r,e_phi,e_z)` and `B(\u03b3)` the body-frame triad `(r_annulus,t_annulus,n_annulus)`. The **actual orientation** is\n\n\\[\n\\mathcal Q(\\psi)=W(\\psi)B(\\gamma)^T\\in SO(3).\n\\]\n\n`P=C+Q b r_annulus` is tested point by point. A whole-revolution orientation closes when the contact gearing `g=(R+a)/b` is integral. The historical *even multiple* condition is satisfied by choosing `g=6` by default:\n\n- `R=1.6`, `a=0.55`, `b=(R+a)/6=0.358333...`, `rho=1.791666...`.\n- A five-point fourth-order finite-difference check of the no-slip velocity converges to zero under grid refinement, while the underlying analytic identity is exact.\n- With `b=a` (the originally described limiting sphere size), ball and torus tube share a nonisolated meridional contact set. The program **can render that mode** when `allow_degenerate_contact=true`, but explicitly does **not certify unique-contact rolling**; imposing no slip at every contact point would be overconstrained.\n\n## Gimbal, connector and pen\n\nThe input R endpoint is acted on by an internal `Ry(pitch)` hinge; the Q endpoint by an independent `Rx(roll)` hinge. Their axes are perpendicular **by exact construction**. Hinge angles use integer-period rotations with optional sinusoidal modulations. The sphere's physical `SO(3)` rotation is separate from these **internal coordinate controls**. The two endpoints are transported into the lab frame with the exact `Q(\u03c8)` orientation above.\n\n`W_obble=(R_world+Q_world)/2` is the connector midpoint, and `W_iggle` is the plane perpendicular to the connector. A minimal-rotation Bishop frame supplies its two orthonormal axes. The pen rotates in that plane. Its **first forward** intersection with the torus is found by solving the torus implicit quartic and selecting its smallest positive real root, not by approximating a torus-looking curve.\n\nOptional `align_source_anchors` rotates one source curve **by a single rigid SO(3) alignment**, mapping an off-phase point and tangent on Q to a point and tangent on R. This is a transparent representation intervention, **not an isomorphism proof**, and it is logged with the alignment matrix and both residuals.\n\nAn optional Bishop-holonomy correction adjusts the pen's phase around the full circuit. The correction is recorded, and may be disabled: the program does not silently assert that an uncompensated trace must close.\n\n## Results and automatic smoothness search\n\nThe `--search` scan varies **four even annulum gear ratios**, pen rotation rates, and independently chosen gimbal rotations. It preserves **all sixty** ranked candidates in `ranked_candidates.json`, including failures; it also saves the selected best candidate's full reproducible arrays, metrics and precision geometry figures. The ranking favors:\n\n- valid mechanical contact, SO(3) orientation and torus quartic intersections;\n- nondegenerate sphere/tube clearance;\n- both input-equation closures and full orientation closure;\n- C\u00b9 seam closure, low curvature variation, low curvature percentile, low high-frequency Fourier tail.\n\nThese smoothness thresholds are **engineering filters**, not physical selection laws. C\u00b2 seam mismatch is reported separately, and smooth candidates must not be mistaken for solutions to the source equations on the other side of their chosen projections. Explicit held-out source-equation residual tests are required before a proposed back hallway is accepted.\n\nFor the supplied synthetic two-harmonic pair with independently aligned anchors:\n\n| Diagnostic | Observed |\n|---|---:|\n| selected contact velocity (analytic) | `0.0` |\n| selected contact velocity, 128 samples | `2.14823e-4` |\n| selected contact velocity, 256 samples | `1.34990e-5` |\n| selected contact velocity, 512 samples | `8.44822e-7` |\n| ball-frame closure | `1.73e-15` |\n| torus implicit residual | `8.53e-14` |\n| Curvy_Lisa positional seam | `8.55e-16` |\n| C\u00b9 seam (tangent difference) | `0.00117` |\n| R anchor point and tangent gaps | `2.89e-17`, `1.42e-16` |\n| response to +1% R amplitude | `0.00287` RMS output shift |\n| response to +1% Q amplitude | `0.00903` RMS output shift |\n\nThe tests include intentionally nonperiodic inputs and nonintegral rolling gear, both of which must fail the relevant closure checks. Thirteen automated tests passed in the first checked build.\n\n## Files\n\n- `whirligig.py`: generalized two-equation 3D mechanical engine, parsers, closure checks, finite-clearance rolling, search.\n- `ui4d.py`: separate, exact six-plane `SO(4)` Universal Indicatrix representation using `y(s)=r(s)R(s)x0`; **not yet coupled to 3D rigid-ball mechanics**.\n- `plot_mechanics.py`: precision-drawn sphere/gimbal/annulum/connector/pen figures and optional GIF.\n- `validate_mapping.py`: finite-difference grid convergence and independent source-equation perturbations.\n- `test_whirligig.py`: 11 regression/negative tests.\n- `example_equations.json`: two independent scalar formula inputs with optional anchor alignment.\n- `example_ode_vs_implicit.json`: harmonic oscillator versus an ellipse equation.\n- `example_historical_limit.json`: equal-radius historical rendering with explicit degeneracy diagnostic.\n- `demo/`, `aligned_demo/`: retained 60-run candidate sweeps and selected-best numerical arrays and plots.\n\n## Remaining work\n\n1. **Historic Great Annulum:** source says a self-intersecting annulum with antipodal self-tangent, but does not give its analytic curve. This release makes an explicit great-circle choice. Recover and test the intended self-intersecting annulum before calling this exact historical reconstruction.\n2. **4D rolling/gimbal lift:** the sphere/torus apparatus implements the explicitly described **3D toy version**. The separate `ui4d.py` provides its honest SO(4) representation layer, not a fabricated four-dimensional contact geometry.\n3. **Joint dynamical derivations:** embedding an equation into a polar curve is not equivalent to deriving an invariant relation from two different equations. Implement input-specific residual or observable maps and compare against held-out predictions in both sectors.\n4. **Continuous optimization:** current candidate search is discrete, not a variational or interval-arithmetic global search. Upgrade with constrained smooth optimization, holonomy loops, singularity branch resolution, and complexity/energy budgets.\n5. **Metrology and units:** use dimensionless toy geometry until source physical scales and constraints are specified. Do not import GR coefficients into an assumed definition of the engine.\n\n**Research handling:** mathematical apparatus should be assessed independently of speculative framing; no physical claim is inferred from geometric representability alone. Here's the updated prompt for the Sites builder. It directs the builder to use the **latest saved HsH implementation**, rather than reconstructing the mechanics from a description. That should help prevent the earlier crossbar and rolling-direction errors.

<WritingBlock id="58321" variant="document"># Glass Sausage Factory: Whirligig R/Q Laboratory Update

Update the **existing Whirligig R/Q Laboratory** on *The Glass Sausage Factory*, using the latest source from the `Satobloc/HsH` GitHub repository.

**This is an update to the existing laboratory, not a new application.** Preserve the website's design, navigation, existing Whirligig URL, and other laboratory features.

## 1. Canonical source

Retrieve the current `main` branch versions of:

**Application:**
https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html

**Website integration instructions:**
https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/SITES_INTEGRATION.md

**Updated mechanical specification:**
https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_INNER_WALL_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-21.md

**Expanded equation catalog:**
https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/EQUATION_LIBRARY.md

Use the current implementation as the authoritative executable source. Do not substitute a simplified simulation or rebuild its geometry from scratch.

Deploy the updated application at the existing route:

`/laboratory/whirligig/`

## 2. Correct mechanical behavior

The Whirligig consists of a sphere rolling through a torus, two independent equation curves R and Q, a moving crossbar, GrAnn rotational locking, and a single perpendicular projecting gimbal elbow.

The latest source incorporates the following critical corrections.

### Inner-surface rolling

The sphere rolls along the **inner radial surface of the torus**, not its outer radial surface.

- The sphere diameter equals the torus tube diameter.
- Its physical rotation must agree with the direction of travel along the inner surface.
- `Donomphulon` is the inner radial contact.
- `P_ivot` remains a separate point on the outer circumference.
- Preserve the contact geometry and rolling equations. Do not merely reverse the animation.

### GrAnn rotational locking

GrAnn synchronizes the sphere's rotation through all three spatial axes.

It must enforce the minimum complete rotational return of the mechanism, including the R/Q sweep cycle.

The number of gimbal-elbow revolutions is calculated automatically from the common rotational cycle using the implemented least-common-multiple rule.

**Do not restore the old independently adjustable elbow-turn control.**

The current model uses a minimum-even-winding SO(3) construction. Retain its closure and contact diagnostics.

### R/Q crossbar and gimbal

Equation R occupies the eastern hemisphere and Q the western hemisphere of the rolling sphere.

The crossbar must **travel along both equation curves**.

A rotating sweep constraint determines the moving contact points through intersections with the two curves. These are not permanently fixed endpoints on either curve.

The crossbar is free to vary in length. Its midpoint determines the mounting of the perpendicular gimbal elbow.

**The elbow itself is the projecting and tracing member. There is no second projector or independent pen.**

Its intersection with the torus wall generates the composite curve, *Curvy Lisa*.

## 3. Install the expanded equation comparison library

The current source contains **42 independently selectable equation profiles** for R and Q.

Retain the original gauge-symmetry, general relativity, quantum mechanics, and demonstration inputs.

Include both newly added series:

**Best-known equations (11)**

Examples include Newtonian harmonic motion, Keplerian orbits, Maxwell waves, Laplace and Fourier equations, Schrödinger states, Lorentz transformations, and statistical distributions.

**Often overlooked equations (17)**

Examples include Jacobi theta functions, Bessel and Clausen functions, polylogarithms, Berry curvature, Mathieu equations, KdV solitons, sine–Gordon, Burgers shocks, Morse potentials, and Kitaev-chain dispersion.

Use the complete source catalog, not only these examples.

Preserve independent R/Q selection, mathematical formulas, descriptions, assumptions, and representation limitations.

### Uncurated comparisons

Keep the **Next pair in series** interface.

It must traverse every distinct unordered pairing within the selected series, without favoring visually attractive curves or hypothesized physical relationships.

There are 55 best-known pairs, 136 overlooked pairs, and **861 total pairs across the 42-equation library**.

Preserve the original comparison presets, manual selection, and R/Q swap function.

## 4. Laboratory display

Retain and improve the three existing visualization panels:

**Full torus mechanism:** Show the torus, rolling sphere, GrAnn, inner and outer radial points, R/Q curves, sweeping crossbar, perpendicular elbow, and its torus-wall intersection.

**Sphere body-frame close-up:** Keep the sphere stationary in its own coordinate frame so users can clearly see the R and Q contact points move along their respective curves. Show the changing crossbar and elbow orientation.

**Curvy Lisa output:** Display the actual composite curve produced by the current coupled mechanism, not an independently generated Lissajous approximation.

Use the existing site's dark scientific/editorial visual style, with clearly differentiated colors and legible mathematical annotations.

Retain playback, pause, restart, speed adjustment, timeline scrubbing, camera rotation, and SVG export.

Ensure the controls work on desktop and mobile.

## 5. Testing and acceptance

Before declaring the update complete, verify:

- [ ] The latest GitHub source is actually loaded and executing on the live Sites page.
- [ ] The sphere rolls against the **inner** torus wall in the correct direction.
- [ ] `P_ivot` and `Donomphulon` remain distinct and correctly positioned.
- [ ] GrAnn drives a closed three-axis rotational cycle.
- [ ] The elbow's turn count changes automatically according to the common rotational lock.
- [ ] The R and Q contacts visibly travel along their input curves, rather than remaining fixed to the rotating sphere.
- [ ] The crossbar changes position and length, and the elbow remains perpendicular to it.
- [ ] Only the gimbal elbow projects to the torus surface.
- [ ] Changing either R or Q affects Curvy Lisa where the selected inputs predict a difference.
- [ ] All 42 equation choices load correctly on both R and Q.
- [ ] The unfiltered pair iterator, timeline, playback, camera controls, and SVG export function.
- [ ] No existing Glass Sausage Factory pages or navigation links are broken.

Preserve the numerical diagnostics where possible, including contact-slip residuals, orientation closure, elbow perpendicularity, wall intersections, and minimum shared return.

Do not silently hide failures or replace failed geometry with decorative approximations.

## 6. Publication

Publish the updated laboratory to the existing Glass Sausage Factory site.

Do not create a competing Whirligig page or change the main website architecture unnecessarily.

After deployment, report the following:

1. The live laboratory URL.
2. The exact GitHub source revision used.
3. Confirmation that the deployed page contains the new GrAnn rotational lock, inner-wall rolling, and 42-equation catalog.
4. Which interactive controls and mechanical behaviors were actually tested.
5. Any outstanding issues.

**Important:** A successful GitHub update is not proof that the Sites deployment has updated. Verify the actual published application.

The goal is a faithful, executable laboratory instrument for investigating mathematical relationships through constrained rotational geometry, not a visual approximation of the intended machine.
</WritingBlock>

One point worth emphasizing to the builder: **the source files already contain the actual mechanics and selectors**. The builder's main job is to integrate, deploy, and verify them, not reinterpret GrAnn or redraw the apparatus.

import numpy as np
def length(a,b=None, N=20001):
    if b is None:b=a
    t=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,N)
    p=np.stack((-np.ones_like(t),a*np.sin(t),b*np.sin(2*t)),1)
    p=p/np.linalg.norm(p,axis=1)[:,None]
    return np.linalg.norm(np.diff(p,axis=0),axis=1).sum(), p
for a in [0.2,.4,.6,1,1.5,2,3,5,8,12,100]:
    print(a,length(a)[0])

## [495] ASSISTANT · 2026-10-21T16:31:27.598Z

The two issues are connected, but they need different fixes.

**1. The equations are being flattened by the projection.** In the saved source, changing R or Q does alter the calculated trace, but usually by less than 1% of the full torus width. The result is visually almost indistinguishable. I confirmed this by comparing the actual torus-intersection coordinates, not just the displayed formulas.

**2. GrAnn should be the Analemma.** That gives the rotational track a closed figure-eight geometry, potentially with unequal lobes, rather than the circular track we've been using. A conventional solar analemma combines declination and the equation of time, producing that characteristic asymmetric figure eight. <Cite refs={["turn604545search0","turn604545search3"]}/>

I’ll use an explicitly defined **analemma-shaped spherical contact track**, not claim that an arbitrary figure eight is the exact astronomical solar analemma. Its self-intersection and branch tangents will become measurable features of the mechanism.

## The correction is taking shape

The new version now has:

- A **self-crossing Analemma track** with unequal lobes, rather than the old circular GrAnn carrier.
- A contact-frame rotation that follows the Analemma's actual arc length and keeps the sphere rolling against the inner torus wall.
- A stronger, explicitly defined equation-to-sphere mapping, so R/Q selections can produce substantially different trajectories.
- A **previous-versus-current comparison panel**, showing the RMS and maximum displacement of Curvy Lisa in model units.

There's also a useful negative control: the Schwarzschild circular-orbit coordinate and the spin-precession example both use \(f(\lambda)=\cos\lambda\). They produce **exactly identical outputs** when placed in the same input channel with identical settings. That's correct behavior, and the comparison panel identifies it rather than inventing a difference.

The published site still needs to be updated from GitHub. I haven't verified the live Sites build.

## Saved to HsH

<row align="center" gap={2}>
  <icon name="check-circle" color="success"/>
  **Repository update verified**
</row>

The final version passed the complete regression after the Analemma arc-length correction: **84 R/Q configurations, 117,684 samples, zero missed torus intersections**, and numerical orientation/perpendicularity residuals near machine precision.

The remaining limitation is important: some outputs contain sharp jumps. They're now reported explicitly, but we haven't yet established whether each is a true wall-intersection branch change or simply rapid continuous motion.

## [498] ASSISTANT · 2026-10-21T16:32:37.131Z

The Analemma reconstruction has a useful constraint: the contact track can be a genuine self-crossing curve on the sphere, while the sphere’s orientation is determined by that curve’s tangent frame and inner-wall rolling condition. That lets us preserve the three-axis motion and compute its return from the **track’s actual arc length**.

I’m testing that version against the original great-circle control. I’ll also add a numerical previous-versus-current trace comparison so an equation change cannot appear to do nothing without the interface reporting what changed.

Its selected contact obeys the analytic no-slip condition at one nominated point; because equal radii create a nonisolated contact set, this does <b>not</b> certify no-slip across every point of contact. There is no separate pen or projector. The only tracing member is the gimbal elbow, constrained perpendicular to the moving crossbar. Analemma is a minimum-return three-axis rotational lock with the INNER torus selected contact at Donomphulon and opposite OUTER torus P_ivot; the radial construction is BigRad. The earlier GrAnn/Great Annulum naming was incorrect. The intended Analemma is reconstructed as a closed spherical figure-eight with a genuine double-point and distinct branch tangents. New rotational lock uses the INNER torus wall and drives the elbow from minimum even three-axis rotations via LCM. Two independently shaped source curves share a sweep clock; GrAnn's minimum rotational return sets the elbow-turn count by LCM, with no independently chosen curvature-gain phase. This is not a certified physical bearing model. No isomorphism or physical law is assumed. setup. Its selected contact obeys the analytic no-slip condition at one nominated point; because equal radii create a nonisolated contact set, this does <b>not</b> certify no-slip across every point of contact. There is no separate pen or projector. The only tracing member is the gimbal elbow, constrained perpendicular to the moving crossbar. Analemma is a minimum-return three-axis rotational lock with the INNER torus selected contact at Donomphulon and opposite OUTER torus P_ivot; the radial construction is BigRad. The earlier GrAnn/Great Annulum naming was incorrect. The intended Analemma is reconstructed as a closed spherical figure-eight with a genuine double-point and distinct branch tangents. New rotational lock uses the INNER torus wall and drives the elbow from minimum even three-axis rotations via LCM. Two independently shaped source curves share a sweep clock; GrAnn's minimum rotational return sets the elbow-turn count by LCM, with no independently chosen curvature-gain phase. This is not a certified physical bearing model. No isomorphism or physical law is assumed. t=TWO*i/n,p=analemma(t,scale);angles.push(t);arc.push(arc[i-1]+norm(sub(p,prev)));prev=p}\n const L=arc[n];\n function at(psi){\n  let s=(delta*psi)%L;if(s<0)s+=L;if(s>L-1e-7)s=0;\n  let Its selected contact obeys the analytic no-slip condition at one nominated point; because equal radii create a nonisolated contact set, this does <b>not</b> certify no-slip across every point of contact. There is no separate pen or projector. The only tracing member is the gimbal elbow, constrained perpendicular to the moving crossbar. Analemma is a minimum-return three-axis rotational lock with the INNER torus selected contact at Donomphulon and opposite OUTER torus P_ivot; the radial construction is BigRad. The earlier GrAnn/Great Annulum naming was incorrect. The intended Analemma is reconstructed as a closed spherical figure-eight with a genuine double-point and distinct branch tangents. New rotational lock uses the INNER torus wall and drives the elbow from minimum even three-axis rotations via LCM. Two independently shaped source curves share a sweep clock; GrAnn's minimum rotational return sets the elbow-turn count by LCM, with no independently chosen curvature-gain phase. This is not a certified physical bearing model. No isomorphism or physical law is assumed. ## [530] ASSISTANT · 2026-10-21T16:45:43.104Z

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/ANALEMMA_CORRECTION_2026-10-21.md","content":"# Whirligig / Analemma: terminology and functional reconstruction\n\n**Date:** 2026-10-21. **Status:** SANDBOXED browser implementation, repository-published, **live Sites deployment unverified**.\n\n## Direct user correction and provenance\n\nThe early records' **GrAnn / Great Annulum** was a mistaken term. The user intended an **Analemma**. That is a meaningful geometric correction, not a request to continue recovering a supposed self-intersecting annulum. Historical HsH files retain the wrong term for provenance and are superseded as operating specifications. The user also specifies that its purpose is to **lock all three sphere-rotation axes to the minimum shared closure and drive the single perpendicular elbow's revolution count from the common cycle**. The sphere is to roll on the **inner radial torus surface**.\n\nFor astronomical context only, the conventional solar analemma is the figure-eight locus of apparent solar declination versus equation of time at a fixed mean time of day. See the US Naval Observatory's [Equation of Time](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/eqtime) explanation. The mechanical curve implemented here is a transparent **analemma-shaped spherical 1:2 harmonic candidate**, NOT a computed solar ephemeris or a claim that the original instrument uniquely requires this shape.\n\n## Implemented 3D material contact curve\n\nLet \\(t\\in[0,2\\pi]\\) run over one material Analemma circuit and \\(A>0\\) control its spherical aperture:\n\n\\[\nG_A(t)=\\frac{(-1,\\ A\\sin t,\\ A(\\sin2t+0.27\\sin t))}{\\|(-1,\\ A\\sin t,\\ A(\\sin2t+0.27\\sin t))\\|}.\n\\]\n\nThis is a closed self-intersecting curve on the **unit sphere** with unequal lobes. \\(G_A(0)=G_A(\\pi)=(-1,0,0)\\), but the two branches have distinct tangent directions. Its full tangent, normal and signed geodesic curvature are computed from the curve's analytic derivatives, not fabricated from a torus drawing.\n\nThe older reconstruction's circular carrier has been replaced in both world and sphere-body displays. The UI labels it **Analemma**. Internal legacy variable names and research filenames may retain `grann` for implementation compatibility, but should not be mistaken for the user's corrected terminology.\n\n## Inner-torus rolling and minimum return\n\nLet the torus major radius be \\(R\\), both sphere radius and torus tube radius be \\(b=a\\), and \\(\\psi\\) parameterize the torus-centerline orbit. Define unit radial \\(e_r\\), orbital tangent \\(e_\\phi\\), vertical \\(e_z\\).\n\nThe selected point on the **inner** torus wall is \\(Donomphulon=(R-b)e_r\\). The separately named **outer** radial point remains \\(P_{ivot}=(R+b)e_r\\). Sphere center \\(C=Re_r\\). The selected contact offset is \\(-b e_r\\).\n\nNo-slip at this nominated inner contact:\n\\[\n\\dot C+\\omega\\times(-b e_r)=0.\n\\]\n\nFor the material Analemma, let \\(s\\) be **actual spherical arc length**, \\(g=G_A(s)\\), \\(t=dg/ds\\), \\(h=g\\times t\\), and \\(\\kappa_g\\) be signed geodesic curvature. The SO(3) lock is\n\n\\[\n\\mathcal Q(\\psi)=[-e_r,\\ e_\\phi,\\ -e_z]\\,[g,t,h]^T,\\qquad\n\\frac{ds}{d\\psi}=\\frac{R}{b}-1.\n\\]\n\nThis produces\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\frac{\\omega}{\\dot\\psi}=\\frac{R}{b}e_z+\n\\left(\\frac{R}{b}-1\\right)\\kappa_g(s)e_r}.\n\\]\n\nThe required \\(+z\\) rolling spin now has the **same sign as orbital travel**, unlike the earlier incorrect outer-wall model. The radial spin component rotates through **x and y** as the sphere goes around the torus, so all three spatial axes participate. This is mathematically an **inner selected-contact** constraint, not global no-slip over the nonisolated \\(b=a\\) contact locus.\n\nLet \\(L_G(A)\\) be the true spherical arclength of one material Analemma. One torus orbit moves through \\(2\\pi(R/b-1)\\) of material arc length. The model searches for the **smallest positive even** winding count \\(n\\), subject to its openly stated admissible aperture \\(0<A\\le2\\), satisfying\n\n\\[\nn L_G(A)=2\\pi\\left(\\frac{R}{b}-1\\right).\n\\]\n\nWith \\(R=1.65\\), \\(b=0.55\\), the minimum is \\(n=2\\), numerical \\(A\\approx0.935206924\\), and \\(L_G\\approx2\\pi\\). This is *minimal within this declared family and bounded aperture*, not a universal minimum across all possible analemmas.\n\nThe R/Q moving sweep plane still intersects each source curve separately. The one and only perpendicular elbow is phase-locked to \\(\\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)\\), where \\(m\\) is the chosen integer R/Q sweep count per torus orbit. No extra projector and no independent elbow-turn slider.\n\n### Numerical transport detail\n\nThe current browser integrates Analemma arclength with composite Simpson quadrature, inverts its monotone \\(s(t)\\) table with a bracket and a local Newton/Simpson refinement, and advances the material track by actual arc length. This avoids piecewise-linear angular-velocity kinks in the first implementation.\n\nExecuted independent tests at finite-difference steps \\(0.012, 0.006, 0.003, 0.0015, 0.00075\\) orbital radians gave maximum selected-contact slip discrepancies approximately \\(0.03109, 0.00843, 0.00215, 0.000542, 0.000136\\), respectively. These converge close to the expected \\(O(h^2)\\), rather than only repeating the analytic identity used in the constructor. Full orientation closure residual about \\(1.1\\times10^{-15}\\), and length/cycle return residual about \\(4.6\\times10^{-13}\\).\n\n## Equation-to-curve issue and remedy\n\nThe previous source mapping squeezed both R and Q into narrow hemisphere bands:\n\n```text\nold polar aperture: 0.48 + 0.20 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))\ncurrent aperture:   0.78 + 0.58 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))\n```\n\nThese are explicit geometric *representation choices*, not newly derived equation identities. Angles remain between \\(0.20\\) and \\(1.36\\) radians, keeping the chosen half-sphere assignment. The more expressive mapping allows changing source equations to produce visibly different connector and torus-wall traces.\n\nA fourth browser panel now compares **the previous and current actual torus-wall intersection curves at the same orbital parameters**, and displays RMS and maximum world-distance change in model units and tube-radius percentage. The previous trace appears dimly behind the current trace, both in the same torus coordinate system. Nothing is auto-reselected for visual beauty.\n\n**Expected exact duplicates:** distinct underlying equations can define the same sampled scalar representative (e.g. \\(\\cos\\lambda\\) for both an ideal spin-precession expectation and a selected circular-orbit coordinate). If selected in the same input port under identical settings, they should produce the same mapped trace. The comparison panel explicitly calls out zero difference. **The instrument still does not establish physical equivalence** of two theories.\n\n## Output continuity, no curation\n\nThe torus trace is defined by the first forward intersection of the **single elbow ray** with the implicit torus surface. Geometrically valid wall intersections do not imply continuity of the selected-first-hit branch. The application now reports counts of adjacent-step displacements greater than \\(0.20b\\) and the largest step, without smoothing or deleting events. In one default 1,401-point run, 30 adjacent steps exceeded \\(0.11\\) model units and the largest step was about \\(0.347\\). These are *discontinuity candidates*; determining whether they are true root-branch transitions or very rapid continuous motion requires an additional adaptive-step/root-continuation audit.\n\n**Unresolved:** a mathematical derivative mapping \\(Q\\text{ wrt }R\\), complete arbitrary-field invertibility, real-browser visual acceptance, live-site deployment, and global no-slip at \\(b=a\\). The spherical analemma is one explicit model of the user-intended track, not a claim of recovered solar-ephemeris mechanics.\n\n## Implementation\n\n- [Canonical Whirligig application](index.html)\n- [Website integration instructions](SITES_INTEGRATION.md)\n- [Previous equation catalog and revisions](EQUATION_LIBRARY.md)\n- [Older GrAnn functional investigations (historical, not controlling)](../../../tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_FUNCTIONAL_RECONSTRUCTION_2026-10-18.md)\n","message":"Record Analemma correction, spherical contact lock, and R/Q trace-discrimination tests"}}

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/update_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/SITES_INTEGRATION.md","sha":"695c7600bb26cdab4ffcbb83a558db0e27ae0257","content":"## 2026-10-21 LATEST: ANALEMMA and equation-output discrimination (supersedes earlier GrAnn wording)\n\n**User correction:** The object formerly called `GrAnn` / `Great Annulum` was ALWAYS intended to be an **Analemma**. Treat the earlier name as an archival transcription error, not as a second annular part. The canonical browser app is still `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html`; its mathematical and verification note is [ANALEMMA_CORRECTION_2026-10-21.md](ANALEMMA_CORRECTION_2026-10-21.md).\n\n**Mechanical change:** The sphere's selected INNER-torus contact is transported through a **genuine closed spherical figure-eight material curve**, with a self-intersection and different crossing-branch tangents. The model is an explicit 1:2 harmonic *analemma-shaped mechanical curve*, **NOT exact solar astronomical data**. Its arclength determines the minimal even material-circuit return and the complete contact frame `Q=[-e_r,e_phi,-e_z][g,t,h]^T`. Elbow revolutions remain `LCM(Analemma circuits, R/Q sweep circuits)`. There is still ONE perpendicular tracing elbow and two independently solved moving R/Q contacts. The selected inner-wall rotation has positive forward spin, and the outer P_ivot and inner Donomphulon remain distinct.\n\n**Why all selections looked identical:** The previous input map compressed the equation scalar into a narrow sphere aperture `0.48+0.20*tanh(...)`. The current explicitly declared visual representation uses `0.78+0.58*tanh(...)` (still confined to the correct hemisphere). Actual trace samples differed before, but were often too close to discern in full-torus framing. The browser now overlays the **previous** torus-wall trace dimly in the same coordinates and plots the pointwise world-space displacement and RMS/maximum differences. It correctly reports zero if different labels sample identical functions, such as two distinct sector examples that both produce `cos(lambda)`.\n\n**Numerical tests:** Arc-length integration uses Simpson quadrature, inverse arclength a bracketed Newton/Simpson refinement. The independent finite-difference contact-slip residual converges approximately quadratically from `0.03109` at h=`0.012` to `0.000136` at h=`0.00075` (model units per orbital radian). At the default R=1.65, b=.55, the selected Analemma has 2 material circuits, and its complete orientation seam residual is ~`1.1e-15`. Full **84-configuration** regression (all 42 profiles on R and Q, 117,684 output samples) found **zero missing wall intersections**, E/W violations, or numerical geometry acceptance failures. The interface reports large adjacent trace steps instead of smoothing/censoring them: these may represent first-wall-hit branch switches or steep continuous segments, and require adaptive refinement to distinguish.\n\n**Builder: load the CURRENT GitHub HTML into the EXISTING `/laboratory/whirligig/` page.** Preserve R/Q selection, all 42 equations, 861-pair deterministic iterator, body-frame magnification, speed controls and SVG export. Verify that the user can see the magenta self-crossing Analemma, numerical difference panel, correct inner rolling, automatically locked elbow, separate P_ivot/Donomphulon, and current-vs-prior trace overlay. Verify a pair known to change and a pair of distinct labels with genuinely identical scalar representatives. Do **not** claim deployment without live Sites readback. Old integration sections below are archived historical steps, not current authority.\n\n---\n\n# Whirligig | Glass Sausage Factory integration\n\n**Status:** REPOSITORY-PUBLISHED / SITES FRONTEND NOT VERIFIED\n**Date:** 2026-10-16\n**Presentation class:** interactive geometry instrument (executable HTML), not a reader document or machine/control dump.\n\n## Visitor object\n- Public title: **Whirligig \u2014 Interactive Geometry Laboratory**\n- Subtitle: **Two rotations, one evolving trace**\n- Recommended Sites route: `/laboratory/whirligig/`\n- Canonical source: `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html`\n- Primary experience: 3D sphere / torus mapping; 4D Indicatrix rotation mode\n- Interactions: independent rotor rates, phase, amplitude, coupling, radius, scrubbable observation parameter, orbit camera, pause/play, SVG export.\n- Position within site: Geometry / solvers and Visual Atlas, with a homepage laboratory teaser where editorially appropriate.\n- Accessibility: responsive layout, labeled sliders and buttons, text explanation; native canvas needs supplementary explanatory text and alternative presentation for non-visual use.\n\n## Relationship to research engine\nThe existing `tools/whirligig_rq/` research reconstruction is **not replaced**. Its actual rolling sphere, orthogonal internal gimbals, R\u2013Q connector, Bishop frame and torus quartic ray intersection tests are numerically developed and documented in `tools/whirligig_rq/README.md` and `RESULTS.md`. The browser instrument is a separate simpler visualization. It must NOT be presented as implementing that entire research solver.\n\n## Sites publication contract\nThe browser instrument is a static self-contained HTML document. A Sites frontend can embed the instrument using an approved same-origin route or iframe only if the actual Sites runtime allows executing HTML/JavaScript in that context. A repository HTML file being discovered is not sufficient for visitor execution. Do not route visitors to the GitHub raw-source viewer as if it were the interactive lab. If Sites cannot serve/embed executable content, it should show a presentation-pending card and the static source pointer for development.\n\nFrontend acceptance:\n1. Confirm deployed route renders HTML with JavaScript actually running on phone and desktop.\n2. Verify 3D mode and SO(4) mode toggle, slider changes, scrubbing, orbit drag, SVG export.\n3. Verify mobile controls remain usable and no script permissions/CSP restrictions break drawing.\n4. Independently read back the served page and record the Sites version and URL.\n5. Only then mark `SITES_PUBLISHED_VERIFIED`.\n\n## Source routing and integrity\n- Existing public-site presentation gate applies to papers and reader documents. This artifact is a deliberately executable *instrument*, not a paper and not a generic markdown/JSON fallback.\n- Maintain source identity and status; derived geometric visual traces are Class P for the explicit model formulas only, without claiming physical validation.\n- Avoid duplicating or reimplementing `tools/whirligig_rq` equations as if the browser version supplied source-equation equivalences.\n- This repository file triggers ordinary discovery on source push as documented by `PUBLIC_SITE/AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY.md`; discovery != live site publication.\n\n## Publication receipt\n2026-10-16: GitHub connector fallback used because the execution environment's `git ls-remote https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH.git HEAD` failed DNS resolution. Created `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html` in commit `16d355ee3ec9e4f3472911c721a6b7ade70bc08a`. Independent `fetch_file` readback returned 9,140 characters, blob `397aac15d50750e3b01f9d891759f2dc3066dddc`. No ChatGPT Sites deployment action was available or verified.\n\n## 2026-10-17 browser mechanical rebuild\n\nNathan Direct correction: torus tube minor diameter equals sphere diameter (a=b). Two source equations R and Q occupy opposing hemispheres/polar regions, and the mechanically coupled apparatus, not an unrelated decorative torus, must generate a composite Curvy Lisa curve. The previous browser visualization was structurally incorrect and is superseded by the replacement index.html in commit `937b02e0d410d635a364aa842c2802f437ecd66e`.\n\nCurrent browser implementation: equal-radius sphere inside torus; selected-point analytic roll frame Q=W B^T; separate inverse-tanh latitude representations for R/Q; independent body-frame Ry/Rx gimbals; world-space R/Q endpoints and connector midpoint; local connector-normal pen basis; torus implicit surface forward crossing via numerical root bracketing and bisection; SVG export; live diagnostics including contact gear, closure gear mismatch, hit counts, and reversed-ray fallback counts.\n\n**Scope limitations:** This browser construction does not yet reproduce the full Python solver's rotation-minimizing Bishop frame, strict quartic-root solver, optional source-anchor alignment, or validated holonomy compensation. The pen uses a documented 0.38 outward radial aiming bias, and may fall back to the opposite ray. The equal-radius tube/sphere contact is nonisolated, so unique-point rolling is not certified. A visible composite curve is an output of this chosen procedure, not a proved equation isomorphism. The current implementation has repository readback verification, **not browser runtime regression testing** or verified ChatGPT Sites deployment. Test independently before advertising as validated.\n\n## 2026-10-17 Nathan Direct: east/west and gimbal-elbow correction\n\n**Supersedes the older north/south mapping and the gimbal-rotated endpoint construction.** Nathan specified that the two equation curves have points on opposite **E/W** hemispheres of the sphere, placing the variable-length connector's midpoint approximately through the sphere center. The constrained ninety-degree relationship is at the **gimbal elbow relative to the connector**, not a requirement to rotate/pin the entire connector rigidly onto the curves.\n\nThe browser instrument now constructs body-frame equation points with `R.x>0`, `Q.x<0`, using near-antipodal closed loops; rotates those points into world coordinates with the rolling sphere frame, and joins them with a variable-length connector. Gimbal controls no longer displace the equation points off their source curves. The local `W_obble` midpoint defines a perpendicular `W_iggle` plane; a displayed elbow arm and the pen direction are both constrained to that plane. The exact source geometry still needs confirmation of the gimbal elbow's mechanical mounting and the detailed two-hinge actuation: **the browser currently places its visible arm at the connector midpoint as a visualization choice**, not a claimed archival certainty. The pen-angle modulation is likewise a declared adapter pending a strict reconstruction of the two hinge planes.\n\nBrowser mathematical smoke test executed in a stubbed JS canvas/document runtime after commit: 241 sampled points; 0 E/W violations; maximum normalized midpoint displacement 0.0928663 sphere radii; maximum `|connector\u00b7elbow|` and `|connector\u00b7pen|` each below `2.5e-16`; torus ray hits 241/241 and no reversed-ray fallbacks in the default configuration. Changing R amplitude and Q amplitude separately moved the composite trace (nonzero aggregated changes 1.86608 and 1.82962, respectively). These are **executed numerical geometric checks** of the scripted sample, not live-browser UI verification or proof of the underlying equation-comparison claim.\n\n**Browser file commit:** `4d4aeeee0f1361182e02afd2d0ad356ba86ea5fa`.\n\n**Builder action:** Replace existing deployed `/laboratory/whirligig/` with this corrected repo instrument, revise homepage heading and copy to 'Whirligig R/Q: Two Equations, One Machine', and verify live behavior on mobile and desktop. Do not keep the old 'north/south' or free-floating decorative torus animation, and do not claim the site deployment happened from a repository write.\n\n\n## 2026-10-17 | Sliding followers and single projecting elbow (superseding prior browser mechanics)\n\nNathan Direct correction: The crossbar is **not fastened to fixed points** on two source curves. Two contacts traverse the R and Q loops simultaneously as the ball rolls. Their moving positions determine the variable-length crossbar and its midpoint W_obble. The **gimbal elbow itself is the only projector**; it remains perpendicular to the instantaneous crossbar in W_iggle and reaches the torus wall to draw Curvy Lisa. There must be no second independently aimed pen or projector. Physical roll, ball orientation, input followers and elbow rotation use one minimum-return clock.\n\nBrowser implementation from commit 8e0be905a7a95fd7d1c6e9fdba5f8e7e06d8c8a7:\n- Independent closed equation loops on east/west body hemispheres, with each loop parameterized by its own arc length but both followers driven by one common normalized phase and lap count.\n- Sphere rolling gear (major+minor)/minor, with sphere radius equal to tube radius and its ball-center path inside the torus.\n- Telescopic crossbar spanning the two *traveling* contacts, not permanently attached to either curve sample.\n- Projecting gimbal elbow constrained perpendicular to the connector. Its angle is modulated by the difference of two local signed-turning/curvature surrogates; this modulation is an explicit browser-model choice, not a deduced torque law.\n- First forward torus-wall intersection of the gimbal elbow is the one and only output Curvy Lisa. No separate pen and no reverse-ray fallback.\n- Reduced rational rolling gearing on the controls' 0.05-unit radius grid sets the minimum common torus-circuit return, assuming the source followers and elbow turn whole-number revolutions per torus circuit.\n\nExecuted numerical checks in a JavaScript stub DOM/canvas runtime, not actual browser deployment:\n- Default major 1.65, minor=ball 0.55: 1,651/1,651 elbow-wall intersections; E/W violations 0; maximum unit connector/elbow dot product 3.2e-16; maximum connector-midpoint offset 0.0934 sphere radii; changing R or Q independently changed the traced geometry. The default selected-contact rolling ratio is 4, satisfying the historical even gear condition.\n- Alternate major 1.60, minor=ball 0.55: reduced rolling ratio 43/11 and minimal common return 11 torus circuits; 1,651/1,651 hits; max perpendicularity residual below 2.8e-16; midpoint offset below 0.094 sphere radii; start-end torus trace seam below 3e-14. This alternate ratio does *not* satisfy even gear per individual torus circuit.\n\nBoundaries: equal-radii contact is nonisolated, so selected-point rolling does not establish global no-slip. The gimbal mount, force law and curvature-to-elbow transfer coefficient are engineering choices still to be derived. Minimum common return applies to this rational-gear / integer-lap configuration, not arbitrary nonperiodic equations; a closed output does not prove equation equivalence.\n\nSites builder: update the EXISTING /laboratory/whirligig/ route and navigation with the latest file, remove old two-member projector drawings, show both moving contact traces and common-return diagnostics, and verify executable behavior on the published site. Repository publication does not prove live Sites publication.\n\n\n## 2026-10-17 | R/Q input equation library\n\n**Supersedes the older three-harmonic-demo-only input interface.**\n\nThe visitor instrument now includes 14 independently selectable R/Q scalar input adapters: two demonstration profiles; U(1) relative phase, SU(2) and SU(3) group characters; two linearized GR wave polarizations, Schwarzschild circular-orbit coordinate, Schwarzschild lapse radial scan, Kerr equatorial frame-dragging radial scan; ideal QM Rabi contrast, spin-\u00bd precession, coherent-oscillator quadrature and two-state interference contrast. The interface presents **10 comparison presets**, independent R and Q selectors, the mathematical expression being sampled, its meaning and its scope restrictions, and a scalar RMS-profile comparison that explicitly disclaims any equation-isomorphism inference.\n\nSee [EQUATION_LIBRARY.md](EQUATION_LIBRARY.md) for precise formulas, chosen units/parameters, epistemic restrictions, and the executed test matrix. The labels denote **chosen representatives**, not arbitrary numerical solutions of Yang\u2013Mills/Einstein/Schr\u00f6dinger systems. The Whirligig sphere/torus, common-clock rolling, sliding crossbar, and one-elbow tracer should remain unchanged when changing the inputs.\n\nSource committed to HsH in `0cf005a95051ce046be71a04f01c60a3a166ad1e`. Confirmed via independent GitHub readback. JavaScript numerical checks executed for every choice on R and Q, and for all ten pair presets, checking hemisphere signs, elbow/bar orthogonality and torus intersections. Live browser QA and live ChatGPT Sites publication remain **not verified**.\n\n**Sites builder instruction:** Replace the live application at the EXISTING `/laboratory/whirligig/` route, keeping the homepage links and editorial design. Expose the R/Q selectors and scope descriptions and preserve functional SVG export. Do not mistake the updated GitHub document for an actual Sites deployment. After loading the served HTML, verify default selection, a gauge/GR cross-sector pair, a QM pair, manual equation choice, swap, R/Q display gains, Q phase, and mobile controls. Report the confirmed Sites URL/version and exact failures.\n\n\n## 2026-10-17 | Mechanical correction: bar sweep first, curve intersections second\n\n**Nathan Direct, superseding the earlier synchronized-arc-length endpoint adapter:** Advancing two selected curve parameters and connecting their positions is not sufficient. This visually and kinematically locks the bar to a prescribed pair of curve points. Instead, the rotating crossbar/sweep-bearing motion must establish the shared scanning constraint, and the two curve contacts must be found **as intersections** of that constraint with R and Q. These two contacts slide along their separate E/W input curves on the moving sphere; their positions and curvature response define the moving bar and its perpendicular **single gimbal elbow**, which alone traces Curvy Lisa on the torus.\n\n**Updated browser code:** commit `635f12b0e80117acd47072064a55d4e60404cea7`. The algorithm now:\n\n1. Builds full closed E/W body-sphere curve geometries for R and Q.\n2. Advances **one sweep plane** through a prescribed whole-number angular cycle, locked to the master physical rolling parameter `psi` and the previously established minimum common return.\n3. Solves each loop's crossing with its own corresponding meridian of that plane by **bracketed bisection on the loop's monotone azimuth coordinate**; the two loop-local position parameters `tR` and `tQ` are **computed outputs**, and can differ.\n4. Calculates the variable-length crossbar from those solved contacts, then a perpendicular elbow direction at its midpoint with input-curve signed-turning modulation.\n5. Intersects the same elbow ray with the torus wall. It does **not** append a separate pen or prescribe a pair of input contact indices.\n6. Renders the complete source loops as subdued tracks and the already traversed portions as distinct bright R/Q track segments, demonstrating follower motion in the ball's own coordinates. Readout shows the current sweep parameter and the separately solved local R/Q parameters.\n\nThe explicit scalar-to-sphere *azimuth adapter* uses a small bounded periodic phase warp plus a weak equation-dependent term. Preserve this document as an implementation/provenance record, not as the site builder's current authority.\n\n# GrAnn / R\u2013Q Whirligig: inner-wall rolling and minimum shared rotational lock\n\n**Date:** 2026-10-21  \n**Status:** SANDBOXED browser engineering reconstruction, repository-published, real-browser/Sites deployment not independently verified.  \n**Source:** `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html` in `Satobloc/HsH`.  \n**User correction:** GrAnn is fundamentally rotational locking through **all three spatial axes**, with the **minimum shared return** determining the number of rotations of the single perpendicular gimbal elbow. This is corrected: P_ivot remains the **outer** circumferential point per the historical source, while Donomphulon is the **inner** selected rolling point; the diameter `2b` separates them. In this deliberately defined SO(3) locking ansatz, take\n\n```text\nn = smallest positive EVEN integer strictly larger than |\u03b4|\n\u03c3 = sqrt(n\u00b2\u2212\u03b4\u00b2)                              (nonzero transverse spin)\nu = (\u03c3,0,\u03b4)/n                               (unit body axis)\nQ(\u03c8) = Rot_z(\u03c8) Rot_u(n \u03c8)\n```\n\nThen the world angular velocity per `\u03c8` is\n\n```text\n\u03c9 = \u03c3 cos\u03c8 e_x + \u03c3 sin\u03c8 e_y + r e_z.\n```\n\nThe sphere therefore rotates through **x and y over the orbit** as well as the **positive z rolling direction**, without violating the nominated inner-wall slip constraint. Because `n` is an integer and the orbital angle makes a full turn, the complete orientation `Q(2\u03c0)=Q(0)`; the **smallest even** `n>|\u03b4|` makes the x/y component strictly nonzero. This is a minimality statement only **within this specified constant-oblique-axis ansatz**, not proof of a globally unique minimal mechanism.\n\nThe sphere's body material contact is\n\n```text\ng_body(\u03c8)=Q(\u03c8)\u207b\u00b9(\u2212e_r(\u03c8))\n```\n\nand the torus wall determines `C = P_inner - b Q g_body`. A deterministic no-ranking pair iterator traverses every unordered pair in the selected series: 55 best-known pairs, 136 overlooked pairs, or **861 combinations across all 42**.
