The archive also contains extensive mathematical derivations, calculations, computational experiments, geometric constructions, revisions, and attempted formalizations.<br><br>\n<strong>Those mathematical results have not yet received comprehensive independent expert vetting.</strong> Some have been checked repeatedly by LLMs or computational tools; some have partial or preliminary review; others remain queued for examination. We do not treat polished presentation, repeated derivation, or agreement among AI systems as a substitute for qualified human review or formal verification.<br><br>\nRather than hide that uncertainty, this library exposes it. Each major document carries a <strong>vetting status</strong> showing what kinds of review have actually occurred, and those statuses will be updated as derivations are recovered, reproduced, challenged, formally checked, or reviewed by specialists.<br><br>\nThe archive is here to be read, tested, criticized, corrected, and improved.\n</td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\n<!-- CONVERSATION_VIEWER_FRONTDOOR_START -->\n## \ud83d\udd0e Development conversations: open by design\n\nIn the interests of maximum transparency, and in the spirit of SAT's **Glass Sausage Factory Ethos**, much of the project's development is available in the form in which it actually happened: conversation. Because SAT/H(s)H has been developed largely through extended dialogue, those exchanges are part of the working record\u2014ideas, mistakes, revisions, dead ends, and all.\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td align=\"center\" width=\"100%\">\n<br>\n<strong>\u25b6 <a href=\"https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/\">OPEN THE H(s)H CONVERSATION VIEWER</a></strong><br><br>\n<em>Interactive viewer thumbnail coming here.</em><br><br>\n<code>[ conversation viewer preview ]</code><br><br>\n<small>Browse, search, replay, and jump to marked moments in the development record.</small><br><br>\n</td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n<!-- CONVERSATION_VIEWER_FRONTDOOR_END -->\n\n<!-- AUTO_FEATURED_START -->\n<!-- FEATURED_SPOTLIGHT:NEW_PAPERS/SEPTEMER_2026/PAPER_PIPELINE.md -->\n## \u2b50 FEATURED \u2014 September 2026\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td>\n<strong>Current spotlight</strong><br><br>\n<a href=\"NEW_PAPERS/SEPTEMER_2026/PAPER_PIPELINE.md\"><strong>PAPER_PIPELINE.md</strong></a><br><br>\n<small>Randomly selected from the current September 2026 featured papers.</small>\n</td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\n**All current featured papers:** [H(s)H TEMPORAL ISOTROPY.txt](NEW_PAPERS/SEPTEMER_2026/H%28s%29H%20TEMPORAL%20ISOTROPY.txt) \u00b7 [H(s)H TIME RESIDUALS.txt](NEW_PAPERS/SEPTEMER_2026/H%28s%29H%20TIME%20RESIDUALS.txt) \u00b7 [PAPER_PIPELINE.md](NEW_PAPERS/SEPTEMER_2026/PAPER_PIPELINE.md) \u00b7 [RECOIL_PREDICTION.pdf](NEW_PAPERS/SEPTEMER_2026/RECOIL_PREDICTION.pdf) \u00b7 [newPAPER.pdf](NEW_PAPERS/SEPTEMER_2026/newPAPER.pdf)\n\n<small>Anything added to <code>NEW_PAPERS/SEPTEMER_2026</code> appears here automatically. The spotlight reshuffles when the folder changes and once daily.</small>\n<!-- AUTO_FEATURED_END -->\n\nH(s)H is the current finite-core/worldtube continuation of the SAT research program. The project starts from a literal geometric reading of Minkowski spacetime and asks how far the known structure of physics can be recovered by following the geometry, projection, motion, coiling, braiding, and interaction rules before importing additional interpretive machinery.\n\nThe images below are not decorative. They are the fastest way into the construction. They show the recurring picture that runs through the SAT record: a trajectory through four-dimensional geometry, its intersection/readout on a time surface, increasing structural complexity through coiling and braiding, and the extension of the same grammar from particle-scale structures to interaction and cosmology.\n\n## Read the theory\n\n**For substantive theory work, begin with [BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md).** The links below are primary/historical theory sources routed through that control surface; being listed here does not independently establish their current premise status.\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><strong>Bedrock / premise state</strong><br><a href=\"BEDROCK.md\">BEDROCK.md</a><br><small>Central theory control surface; start here.</small></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><strong>Foundational source</strong><br><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/THE%20FUNDAMENTAL%20INTUITIONS%20%E2%80%94%20EXTENDED.pdf\">The Fundamental Intuitions \u2014 Extended</a><br><small>Foundational conceptual doctrine; see BEDROCK for current routing/status.</small></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><strong>Historical formal SAT</strong><br><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/FULL_THEORY.pdf\">FULL_THEORY.pdf</a><br><small>Historical/formal SAT presentation; not automatic current bedrock.</small></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><strong>Derivation / provenance</strong><br><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/..%5B%F0%9F%8E%9B%EF%B8%8F_NATHAN_DASH%5D/..Derivation_Index.md\">Derivation index</a><br><small>Archive/provenance map; evidence routing rather than theory authority.</small></td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\n> **Important:** `synthesis/CURRENT_SYNTHESIS.md` is not a controlling theory surface. Current premise authority/status belongs in BEDROCK unless a newer Nathan Direct instruction says otherwise.\n\n> **Read the pictures first if you want the fastest conceptual route. Read BEDROCK first if you are going to build on the theory.**\n\n---\n\n## 1. One geometric construction, many familiar descriptions\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/01_unified_geometric_vision.jpg\" alt=\"Unified geometric vision: QCD, relativity and string-like descriptions arising from one filament/time-surface geometry\" width=\"100%\"></a>\n\nSAT's organizing move is not to invent a separate geometric story for every physical sector. It asks whether familiar descriptions can be understood as different projections, interaction regimes, or effective descriptions of one underlying geometric construction. The labels in historical figures should be read as **SAT mappings and research claims**, not as a substitute for the standard theories themselves.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Particle differences as differences of geometry\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/02_particle_spectrum_geometry.jpg\" alt=\"Spectrum of particles from a spectrum of geometry\" width=\"100%\"></a>\n\nA recurring SAT idea is that the apparent catalog of particle types may be reorganized as a catalog of trajectory geometries: simple traveling excitation, persistent coiling, and increasingly interdependent or braided structures. The current H(s)H program is working to replace the simplified centerline picture with a finite-core worldtube treatment while preserving the same geometric dependency structure.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The basic readout: trajectory and time-surface intersection\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/03_helix_time_plane_intersection.jpg\" alt=\"Helical trajectory intersecting a time surface\" width=\"78%\"></a>\n\nThe basic visual grammar is a higher-dimensional trajectory intersecting a lower-dimensional time slice or readout surface. The intersection can move, rotate, close, open, or change shape even when the underlying trajectory remains continuous.\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/04_theta4_tangent_time_normal.jpg\" alt=\"Worldline tangent, time-field normal, and theta angle\" width=\"78%\"></a>\n\nHistorically SAT used an angular measure, usually written **\u03b8\u2084**, to track the orientation of the trajectory relative to the time direction/surface normal. The notation and exact formal role have evolved; the geometric relationship is the durable part of the picture.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Not just a straight helix: recursion and carrier geometry\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/05_recursive_helix_curved_carrier.jpg\" alt=\"Recursive helix following a curved carrier\" width=\"76%\"></a>\n\nThe model is not simply \"everything is a helix.\" A local coil may itself propagate along a curved carrier, and that carrier may participate in still larger-scale structure. The present H(s)H work is focused on making this recursive, finite-core geometry explicit rather than leaving it compressed into a worldline skeleton.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Interaction as geometric braiding\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/06_qcd_geometric_braiding.jpg\" alt=\"QCD analogy represented by geometric braiding\" width=\"100%\"></a>\n\nSAT's braid-centered interaction picture treats multi-filament organization as a geometric relation rather than merely adding a new label to otherwise independent particles. In the historical worldline model this was represented by interweaving centerlines; H(s)H asks what the corresponding finite-core worldtube mechanics actually are: **bundle geometry + finite extent + intersection/readout + deformation**.\n\n---\n\n## 6. A worldline can generate an evolving family of observed patterns\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/08_worldline_time_slice_evolution.jpg\" alt=\"Worldline propagation through successive time slices producing evolving geometric patterns\" width=\"76%\"></a>\n\nSuccessive slices through one continuous construction need not look alike. SAT repeatedly uses this fact to distinguish the full trajectory from the lower-dimensional pattern available at any one slice. The same distinction is central to the move from worldline to worldtube.\n\n---\n\n## 7. The construction is intended to close at cosmological scale\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/09_geometric_cosmology_expansion.jpg\" alt=\"SAT geometric cosmology and expansion as resolution\" width=\"100%\"></a>\n\nSAT was developed as a whole-physics translation program rather than a particle model alone. Its historical materials therefore extend the same geometric vocabulary into gravitation, large-scale structure, expansion, fluids, and cosmology. Some specific equations and historical mechanisms have since been revised or retired; the broad structural ambition remains part of H(s)H.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Historical continuity is part of the record\n\nThe public H(s)H repository is not the primary historical archive. The larger [SAT Theory Archive 2023\u201325](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25) preserves the developmental record. The quick provenance window below deliberately spans both ends of that record: surviving 2003 material and the much more explicit 2025 SAT notebooks.\n\n### Earliest surviving notebook/sketch material \u2014 2003\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td width=\"33%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_2003.png\"><img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_2003.png\" alt=\"Earliest surviving 2003 sketch\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"33%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_2003_3.png\"><img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_2003_3.png\" alt=\"Early 2003 geometric sketch\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"33%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_Leuchtturm_notebook_2003.png\"><img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_Leuchtturm_notebook_2003.png\" alt=\"Dated 2003 notebook record\"></a></td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\nThe Archive dates the Ireland-trip notebook period to **February\u2013June 2003** and preserves the surviving sketches as their own source layer. The point here is not to retrofit every later SAT term onto those pages, but to show the early geometric ancestry directly rather than beginning the visual history in 2025.\n\n### Explicit SAT notebook development \u2014 2025\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/PROVENANCE/01_worldlines_notecard.jpg\" alt=\"Historical worldlines sketch\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/PROVENANCE/02_sat_notebook_2025-04-15.jpg\" alt=\"SAT notebook April 15 2025\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/PROVENANCE/03_early_coil_plane_notebook.jpg\" alt=\"SAT coil and plane notebook sketch\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/PROVENANCE/04_sat_notebook_2025-04-25_cropped.png\" alt=\"SAT notebook April 25 2025\"></a></td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\nThe point of preserving the sketches alongside later renderings is not that every current H(s)H statement was already explicit in the earliest work. It is that the **recognizable generative geometry appears early and persists while the physical identifications, mathematical machinery, and resolution of the model accumulate around it**.\n\n[Browse the 2003 sketch folder \u2192](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/2003%20SKETCHES) \u00b7 [Browse the historical SAT visuals \u2192](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS) \u00b7 [Browse the curated H(s)H visual package \u2192](SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/)\n\n---\n\n# History in brief\n\nSAT/H(s)H did not begin as a finished theory and then acquire illustrations afterward. The geometry came first and was repeatedly revisited, renamed, formalized, tested, simplified, and broadened. The historical archive records the path in much greater detail, but several turning points make the overall development legible:\n\n**c. 1991 \u2192 2003\u201304:** Minkowski worldline/timesheet thinking develops into surviving higher-dimensional path, coil, mass and curvature sketches.\n\n**2024:** the old construction is reopened explicitly as Proto-SAT; line/plane and helix/hypersurface geometry becomes the center of sustained theory-building.\n\n**2 February 2025:** the Fundamental Intuitions are presented publicly: physicalized worldlines/filaments, a time surface, particle-as-intersection, and deliberate import of successful Standard Model, relativity and quantum structure.\n\n**Spring\u2013summer 2025:** SAT expands rapidly into an all-physics translation program. \u03b8\u2084, torsion/twist, particle mappings, QCD-like locking/braiding, 4D-covariant integration, Hopf/Borromean structures, SAT-O modules, mathematical-backbone work, prediction protocols and hostile audits all enter the record.\n\n**Late 2025 \u2192 early 2026:** the project becomes increasingly formal and source-conscious: 4DHH, SAT-O, worldline/holonomy work, explicit prediction documents, Lean-oriented rebuilding, provenance tracking, and adversarial validation become central.\n\n**Mid-2026:** the finite-core problem becomes unavoidable. The centerline/filament picture is generalized into **H(s)H \u2014 Hyper(super)Helical Worldtube**, with explicit worldtube cross-section, recursive coiling, braid/bundle geometry, and a cleaner separation between full higher-dimensional structure and lower-dimensional readout.\n\nThe current project is therefore best read neither as a frozen 2025 theory nor as a clean break from it. H(s)H is the attempt to retain the durable geometric grammar while rebuilding the mathematical object at higher resolution.\n\n---\n\n# Reading the archive responsibly\n\nThis repository intentionally mixes several kinds of material that should not be collapsed into one evidentiary category:\n\n- **Nathan-authored conceptual statements** \u2014 primary evidence for what the model is intended to mean.\n- **Historical derivations and calculations** \u2014 evidence of mathematical development, with varying levels of checking.\n- **AI-generated formalizations and reconstructions** \u2014 useful working mathematics, but not automatically authoritative.\n- **Computational experiments** \u2014 evidence for what a particular implementation produced under specified assumptions.\n- **Visualizations** \u2014 often the clearest route into the geometry, but not themselves proofs.\n- **External-source comparisons** \u2014 context for comparison and vocabulary, not evidence that SAT/H(s)H inherits the validity of the compared theory.\n\nThe repository's vetting/status labels are intended to keep those categories visible. Where a document has not yet been independently checked, it should be read as part of an active research record rather than as settled result.\n\n---\n\n# Where to go next\n\nFor theory work, return to **[BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md)**. For historical reconstruction, use the **[SAT Theory Archive 2023\u201325](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25)** and the derivation/provenance indices. For development conversations, use the **[Conversation Viewer](https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/)**. For operations, coordination, automation, and infrastructure, use **[WORKSPACES/COMMON](WORKSPACES/COMMON/)**.","message":"Remove the unrequested public-site route from the repository landing page"}}

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"tools/build_whirligig_pages.py","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Assemble the existing Conversation Viewer with the standalone Whirligig route.\n\nThe Viewer remains the project-site root. This build adds exactly one instrument\nroute and does not create or replace a public-site homepage.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport re\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\nUNIVERSAL_LINK = re.compile(\n    r'\\s*\u00b7\\s*<a href=\"\\.\\./universal-indicatrix/index\\.html\"[^>]*>'\n    r'Universal Indicatrix \\(blind lab\\)</a>'\n)\n\nREQUIRED_MARKERS = (\n    \"Whirligig\", \"Analemma\", \"Donomphulon\", \"P_ivot\", \"Curvy Lisa\",\n    \"pairPreset\", \"differenceStatus\",\n)\n\n\ndef build(root: Path, output: Path) -> Path:\n    root = root.resolve()\n    viewer = root / \"CONVERSATION_VIEWER\"\n    instrument = root / \"PUBLIC_SITE\" / \"instruments\" / \"whirligig\" / \"index.html\"\n    output = output.resolve()\n\n    if not (viewer / \"index.html\").is_file():\n        raise FileNotFoundError(\"Existing Conversation Viewer root is missing\")\n    if not instrument.is_file():\n        raise FileNotFoundError(\"Canonical Whirligig instrument source is missing\")\n    if output.exists():\n        raise FileExistsError(f\"Refusing to overwrite existing build directory: {output}\")\n    if output == root or root in output.parents is False:\n        raise ValueError(\"Build output must be a new directory inside the repository root\")\n\n    html = instrument.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    missing = [marker for marker in REQUIRED_MARKERS if marker not in html]\n    if missing:\n        raise ValueError(\"Whirligig source failed content checks: \" + \", \".join(missing))\n\n    # The canonical instrument includes a sibling Universal Indicatrix link.\n    # This build intentionally publishes Whirligig only, so suppress that\n    # one unavailable sibling link in the generated copy, not in source.\n    html, removed = UNIVERSAL_LINK.subn(\"\", html)\n    if removed != 1:\n        raise ValueError(f\"Expected exactly one sibling instrument link, found {removed}\")\n    if \"../universal-indicatrix/index.html\" in html:\n        raise ValueError(\"Generated Whirligig page still contains an unpublished sibling route\")\n\n    shutil.copytree(viewer, output)\n    route = output / \"laboratory\" / \"whirligig\"\n    route.mkdir(parents=True)\n    (route / \"index.html\").write_text(html, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    # Carry any future instrument-local assets without changing the Viewer.\n    assets = instrument.parent / \"assets\"\n    if assets.is_dir():\n        shutil.copytree(assets, route / \"assets\")\n\n    if not (output / \"index.html\").is_file():\n        raise RuntimeError(\"Viewer root was not preserved in the output\")\n    if not (route / \"index.html\").is_file():\n        raise RuntimeError(\"Whirligig route was not created\")\n    if (output / \"glass-sausage-factory\").exists():\n        raise RuntimeError(\"Unexpected replacement homepage appeared in output\")\n\n    return route / \"index.html\"\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--root\", type=Path, default=Path(\".\"))\n    parser.add_argument(\"--output\", type=Path, default=Path(\"_site\"))\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    result = build(args.root, args.output)\n    print(f\"Built Whirligig route: {result}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n","message":"Add a narrow Pages builder for the standalone Whirligig route"}}

They show the recurring picture that runs through the SAT record: a trajectory through four-dimensional geometry, its intersection/readout on a time surface, increasing structural complexity through coiling and braiding, and the extension of the same grammar from particle-scale structures to interaction and cosmology.\n\n## Read the theory\n\n**For substantive theory work, begin with [BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md).** The links below are primary/historical theory sources routed through that control surface; being listed here does not independently establish their current premise status.\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><strong>Bedrock / premise state</strong><br><a href=\"BEDROCK.md\">BEDROCK.md</a><br><small>Central theory control surface; start here.</small></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><strong>Foundational source</strong><br><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/THE%20FUNDAMENTAL%20INTUITIONS%20%E2%80%94%20EXTENDED.pdf\">The Fundamental Intuitions \u2014 Extended</a><br><small>Foundational conceptual doctrine; see BEDROCK for current routing/status.</small></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><strong>Historical formal SAT</strong><br><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/FULL_THEORY.pdf\">FULL_THEORY.pdf</a><br><small>Historical/formal SAT presentation; not automatic current bedrock.</small></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><strong>Derivation / provenance</strong><br><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/..%5B%F0%9F%8E%9B%EF%B8%8F_NATHAN_DASH%5D/..Derivation_Index.md\">Derivation index</a><br><small>Archive/provenance map; evidence routing rather than theory authority.</small></td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\n> **Important:** `synthesis/CURRENT_SYNTHESIS.md` is not a controlling theory surface. Read BEDROCK first if you are going to build on the theory.**\n\n---\n\n## 1. One geometric construction, many familiar descriptions\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/01_unified_geometric_vision.jpg\" alt=\"Unified geometric vision: QCD, relativity and string-like descriptions arising from one filament/time-surface geometry\" width=\"100%\"></a>\n\nSAT's organizing move is not to invent a separate geometric story for every physical sector. It asks whether familiar descriptions can be understood as different projections, interaction regimes, or effective descriptions of one underlying geometric construction. The labels in historical figures should be read as **SAT mappings and research claims**, not as a substitute for the standard theories themselves.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Particle differences as differences of geometry\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/02_particle_spectrum_geometry.jpg\" alt=\"Spectrum of particles from a spectrum of geometry\" width=\"100%\"></a>\n\nA recurring SAT idea is that the apparent catalog of particle types may be reorganized as a catalog of trajectory geometries: simple traveling excitation, persistent coiling, and increasingly interdependent or braided structures. The current H(s)H program is working to replace the simplified centerline picture with a finite-core worldtube treatment while preserving the same geometric dependency structure.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The basic readout: trajectory and time-surface intersection\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/03_helix_time_plane_intersection.jpg\" alt=\"Helical trajectory intersecting a time surface\" width=\"78%\"></a>\n\nThe basic visual grammar is a higher-dimensional trajectory intersecting a lower-dimensional time slice or readout surface. The intersection can move, rotate, close, open, or change shape even when the underlying trajectory remains continuous.\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/04_theta4_tangent_time_normal.jpg\" alt=\"Worldline tangent, time-field normal, and theta angle\" width=\"78%\"></a>\n\nHistorically SAT used an angular measure, usually written **\u03b8\u2084**, to track the orientation of the trajectory relative to the time direction/surface normal. The notation and exact formal role have evolved; the geometric relationship is the durable part of the picture.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Not just a straight helix: recursion and carrier geometry\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/05_recursive_helix_curved_carrier.jpg\" alt=\"Recursive helix following a curved carrier\" width=\"76%\"></a>\n\nThe model is not simply \"everything is a helix.\" A local coil may itself propagate along a curved carrier, and that carrier may participate in still larger-scale structure. The present H(s)H work is focused on making this recursive, finite-core geometry explicit rather than leaving it compressed into a worldline skeleton.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Interaction as geometric braiding\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/06_qcd_geometric_braiding.jpg\" alt=\"QCD analogy represented by geometric braiding\" width=\"100%\"></a>\n\nSAT's braid-centered interaction picture treats multi-filament organization as a geometric relation rather than merely adding a new label to otherwise independent particles. In the historical worldline model this was represented by interweaving centerlines; H(s)H asks what the corresponding finite-core worldtube mechanics actually are: **bundle geometry + finite extent + intersection/readout + deformation**.\n\n---\n\n## 6. A worldline can generate an evolving family of observed patterns\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/08_worldline_time_slice_evolution.jpg\" alt=\"Worldline propagation through successive time slices producing evolving geometric patterns\" width=\"76%\"></a>\n\nSuccessive slices through one continuous construction need not look alike. SAT repeatedly uses this fact to distinguish the full trajectory from the lower-dimensional pattern available at any one slice. The same distinction is central to the move from worldline to worldtube.\n\n---\n\n## 7. The construction is intended to close at cosmological scale\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/FRONT_PAGE/09_geometric_cosmology_expansion.jpg\" alt=\"SAT geometric cosmology and expansion as resolution\" width=\"100%\"></a>\n\nSAT was developed as a whole-physics translation program rather than a particle model alone. Its historical materials therefore extend the same geometric vocabulary into gravitation, large-scale structure, expansion, fluids, and cosmology. Some specific equations and historical mechanisms have since been revised or retired; the broad structural ambition remains part of H(s)H.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Historical continuity is part of the record\n\nThe public H(s)H repository is not the primary historical archive. The larger [SAT Theory Archive 2023\u201325](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25) preserves the developmental record. The quick provenance window below deliberately spans both ends of that record: surviving 2003 material and the much more explicit 2025 SAT notebooks.\n\n### Earliest surviving notebook/sketch material \u2014 2003\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td width=\"33%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_2003.png\"><img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_2003.png\" alt=\"Earliest surviving 2003 sketch\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"33%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_2003_3.png\"><img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_2003_3.png\" alt=\"Early 2003 geometric sketch\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"33%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_Leuchtturm_notebook_2003.png\"><img src=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/2003%20SKETCHES/Earliest_Surviving_Sketches_Leuchtturm_notebook_2003.png\" alt=\"Dated 2003 notebook record\"></a></td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\nThe Archive dates the Ireland-trip notebook period to **February\u2013June 2003** and preserves the surviving sketches as their own source layer. The point here is not to retrofit every later SAT term onto those pages, but to show the early geometric ancestry directly rather than beginning the visual history in 2025.\n\n### Explicit SAT notebook development \u2014 2025\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/PROVENANCE/01_worldlines_notecard.jpg\" alt=\"Historical worldlines sketch\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/PROVENANCE/02_sat_notebook_2025-04-15.jpg\" alt=\"SAT notebook April 15 2025\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/PROVENANCE/03_early_coil_plane_notebook.jpg\" alt=\"SAT coil and plane notebook sketch\"></a></td>\n<td width=\"25%\" valign=\"top\"><a href=\"https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS\"><img src=\"SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/PROVENANCE/04_sat_notebook_2025-04-25_cropped.png\" alt=\"SAT notebook April 25 2025\"></a></td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\nThe point of preserving the sketches alongside later renderings is not that every current H(s)H statement was already explicit in the earliest work. It is that the **recognizable generative geometry appears early and persists while the physical identifications, mathematical machinery, and resolution of the model accumulate around it**.\n\n[Browse the 2003 sketch folder \u2192](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/2003%20SKETCHES) \u00b7 [Browse the historical SAT visuals \u2192](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS) \u00b7 [Browse the curated H(s)H visual package \u2192](SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/)\n\n---\n\n# History in brief\n\nSAT/H(s)H did not begin as a finished theory and then acquire illustrations afterward. The geometry came first and was repeatedly revisited, renamed, formalized, tested, simplified, and broadened. The historical archive records the path in much greater detail, but several turning points make the overall development legible:\n\n**c. 1991 \u2192 2003\u201304:** Minkowski worldline/timesheet thinking develops into surviving higher-dimensional path, coil, mass and curvature sketches.\n\n**2024:** the old construction is reopened explicitly as Proto-SAT; line/plane and helix/hypersurface geometry becomes the center of sustained theory-building.\n\n**2 February 2025:** the Fundamental Intuitions are presented publicly: physicalized worldlines/filaments, a time surface, particle-as-intersection, and deliberate import of successful Standard Model, relativity and quantum structure.\n\n**Spring\u2013summer 2025:** SAT expands rapidly into an all-physics translation program. \u03b8\u2084, torsion/twist, particle mappings, QCD-like locking/braiding, 4D-covariant integration, Hopf/Borromean structures, SAT-O modules, mathematical-backbone work, prediction protocols and hostile audits all enter the record.\n\n**Late 2025 \u2192 early 2026:** the project becomes increasingly formal and source-conscious: 4DHH, SAT-O, worldline/holonomy work, explicit prediction documents, Lean-oriented rebuilding, provenance tracking, and adversarial validation become central.\n\n**Mid-2026:** the finite-core problem becomes unavoidable. The centerline/filament picture is generalized into **H(s)H \u2014 Hyper(super)Helical Worldtube**, with explicit worldtube cross-section, recursive coiling, braid/bundle geometry, and a cleaner separation between full higher-dimensional structure and lower-dimensional readout.\n\nThe current project is therefore best read neither as a frozen 2025 theory nor as a clean break from it. H(s)H is the attempt to retain the durable geometric grammar while rebuilding the mathematical object at higher resolution.\n\n---\n\n# Reading the archive responsibly\n\nThis repository intentionally mixes several kinds of material that should not be collapsed into one evidentiary category:\n\n- **Nathan-authored conceptual statements** \u2014 primary evidence for what the model is intended to mean.\n- **Historical derivations and calculations** \u2014 evidence of mathematical development, with varying levels of checking.\n- **AI-generated formalizations and reconstructions** \u2014 useful working mathematics, but not automatically authoritative.\n- **Computational experiments** \u2014 evidence for what a particular implementation produced under specified assumptions.\n- **Visualizations** \u2014 often the clearest route into the geometry, but not themselves proofs.\n- **External-source comparisons** \u2014 context for comparison and vocabulary, not evidence that SAT/H(s)H inherits the validity of the compared theory.\n\nThe repository's vetting/status labels are intended to keep those categories visible. Where a document has not yet been independently checked, it should be read as part of an active research record rather than as settled result.\n\n---\n\n# Where to go next\n\nFor theory work, return to **[BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md)**. For historical reconstruction, use the **[SAT Theory Archive 2023\u201325](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25)** and the derivation/provenance indices. For development conversations, use the **[Conversation Viewer](https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/)**. For operations, coordination, automation, and infrastructure, use **[WORKSPACES/COMMON](WORKSPACES/COMMON/)**.","message":"Restore the original repository entry-point navigation"}}

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/update_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"PUBLIC_SITE/SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md","sha":"9dd69a4cfca46b6bde27784488b0bd312c049497","content":"# Glass Sausage Factory \u2014 Site Development Work Log\n\n**Status:** ACTIVE continuity record  \n**Scope:** public-site design, information architecture, presentation, asset intake, and publishing handoff  \n**Established:** 2026-09-20 by Nathan directive  \n**Authority:** operational/editorial only; this log does not define theory truth\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis file is the durable handoff surface for development of the Glass Sausage Factory public site.\n\nUse it so that site work does not depend on one ChatGPT/site-builder conversation retaining context. Any instance taking over site development should read this file together with:\n\n- `PUBLIC_SITE/README.md`\n- `PUBLIC_SITE/EDITORIAL_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md`\n- `PUBLIC_SITE/CURRENT_WORK.json`\n- `PUBLIC_SITE/NEWS_FEED.json`\n- `PUBLIC_SITE/ASSET_MANIFEST.json`\n- the current repo orientation/control documents when theory-state or current-work claims are involved.\n\nThis log records decisions, current state, open work, and publishing limitations. It should be updated whenever a site-development session makes a material design, architecture, content-feed, or publication decision.\n\n---\n\n## Current site target\n\n**Public site:** Glass Sausage Factory  \n**Known current published URL:** `https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site`\n\nThe published page and the repository-side public-site infrastructure are separate surfaces. Repository work should be treated as durable source/state for future site-builder sessions. Do **not** claim that a repository edit has changed the live site unless the publishing surface was actually available and used.\n\n---\n\n# 2026-09-20 \u2014 continuity baseline\n\n## Repository-side infrastructure now in place\n\n`PUBLIC_SITE/` contains durable feeds and design guidance for the public presentation:\n\n- `CURRENT_WORK.json` \u2014 current-work feed.\n- `FEATURED_QUOTES.json` \u2014 current curated quote feed.\n- `quote_candidates/` \u2014 quote nomination lane.\n- `NEWS_FEED.json` \u2014 rotating source-linked external-news feed.\n- `news_candidates/` \u2014 news/source-recovery intake.\n- `EDITORIAL_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` \u2014 active visual/editorial guidance.\n- `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` \u2014 visual asset registry.\n- `README.md` \u2014 public-site content architecture and source discipline.\n\nA shared worker assignment exists at:\n\n- `WORKSPACES/COMMON/ASSIGNMENT_PUBLIC_SITE_ROTATING_FEATURES_2026-09-20.md`\n\n### Quote workflow ownership update\n\nNathan has assigned **Tern** to update the broader workflow so that quote capture becomes a standing project behavior.\n\nSite-development instances should therefore **consume** the resulting quote pipeline rather than independently redesigning or competing with Tern's workflow. Existing public-site quote guidance should be treated as provisional wherever Tern establishes a newer shared workflow standard.\n\nThe site-facing responsibility remains:\n\n- display/rotation behavior;\n- visual treatment;\n- source/context display;\n- placement across relevant pages;\n- integration with stable archive/source links.\n\n---\n\n## Editorial posture\n\nCurrent target:\n\n**neutral, intriguing, source-forward, scientifically literate, and confident about the existence of the work without overselling what the work establishes.**\n\nAvoid default defensive or self-deprecating framing. Ordinary uncertainty belongs in concise status/provenance metadata, not in repeated apology language.\n\nPreferred explanatory rhythm:\n\n**interesting object \u2192 what it says/does \u2192 why it matters here \u2192 source/status**\n\nThe public presentation should make the project readable without converting presentation polish into epistemic authority.\n\n---\n\n## Visual direction \u2014 revised after Nathan image batch, 2026-09-20\n\nNathan supplied a substantial visual batch in the site-development conversation. ## [1062] ASSISTANT · 2026-11-02T05:41:24.019Z

That establishes an important geometric constraint, and it exposes a fundamental problem with the current Analemma implementation.

I checked the original *Finding the Donut* archive, page 26. It describes two distinct features:

1. The **crosspoint**, where the Analemma intersects itself.
2. A separate **self-tangency at the antipode** of that crosspoint.

Your new description gives those features a definite orientation:

- **North and South:** the two projected-curve directions.
- **East:** the Analemma's transverse waist crossing.
- **West:** the antipodal kissing point, where the two branches share a tangent.

The two self-contact points must be exactly antipodal, not merely opposite-looking points in a drawing.

**The existing implementation cannot do this.** Its curve is

\[
G_A(t)=
\frac{(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin 2t+0.27\sin t))}
{\|(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin 2t+0.27\sin t))\|}
\]

Its first coordinate is always negative. Consequently, it cannot contain an antipodal pair. This is a geometric incompatibility, not a rendering problem.

One coordinate decision before I alter the implementation: should I now move the R and Q projected curves from their existing east/west hemispheres to the **north/south hemispheres**, superseding the earlier R-east/Q-west arrangement? <MemoryCite />

That determines how the Analemma, moving followers, crossbar, and contact frame must be oriented together.

- **Analemma crossing:** at the east equatorial pole, \(E=(1,0,0)\).
- **Analemma kissing point:** at the antipodal west equatorial pole, \(W=(-1,0,0)\).
- **Figure-eight lobes:** one loops around the north pole in the northern hemisphere; the other loops around the south pole in the southern hemisphere.

That supersedes the earlier east–west assignment for R and Q. The important geometric relationship is that the projected curves use one antipodal pair of poles, while the Analemma's crossing and tangency use the other.

A cleaner spherical construction now satisfies the topology without putting the Analemma *through* either pole. Let the sphere have unit radius and define

\[
\begin{aligned}
\beta(t)&=\kappa\sin t\cos^2t,\\
A_\kappa(t)&=
\bigl(
\cos\beta(t)\cos 2t,\;
\cos\beta(t)\sin 2t,\;
\sin\beta(t)
\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

Here \(\beta\) is latitude, \(2t\) is longitude, and \(\kappa\) controls how far the two lobes reach toward their respective poles.

This construction has the required features:

- The northern lobe, \(0<t<\pi\), stays in the northern hemisphere and winds once around the north pole.
- The southern lobe, \(\pi<t<2\pi\), stays in the southern hemisphere and winds once around the south pole.
- The branches meet transversely at east, \(E\), and kiss tangentially at west, \(W\).
- The poles remain inside their respective loops rather than lying on the Analemma itself.

The important distinction is that this is a **spherical figure-eight with two distinct antipodal contact types**, not merely a planar figure-eight projected onto a sphere.

There is one mechanical consequence to settle before I alter the rotational-lock code.

Because east and west are antipodes, each lobe must contain two arcs connecting points at least \(\pi\) apart. A genuine crossing at east and a distinct tangential kiss at west make the total Analemma length **strictly greater than \(4\pi\)** on the unit sphere. Each individual lobe is therefore longer than \(2\pi\).

The current default has \(R/b=3\). Under the existing inner-wall rolling constraint, the material point travels

\[
2\pi(R/b-1)=4\pi
\]

per torus orbit. That is exactly the degenerate lower bound, leaving no length for a nondegenerate Analemma while preserving an even circuit count.

The original archive says “an even multiple of circuits along GrAnn,” but doesn't unambiguously define *circuit* here. **Did you intend one circuit to mean one lobe, or one complete traversal of the entire two-lobed Analemma?**

That distinction changes the required torus ratio: the first interpretation needs \(R/b>3\); the second needs \(R/b>5\), under the present rolling model. I don't want to silently change the gearing or weaken the geometry to make the numbers fit.

I'll hold the Whirligig code changes until that distinction is settled.

import numpy as np, math
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

def analemma(t,kappa=3.0):
    beta=kappa*np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**2
    lam=2*t
    cb=np.cos(beta)
    return np.stack([cb*np.cos(lam), cb*np.sin(lam), np.sin(beta)], axis=-1)

def beta_fn(t,k=3.0):
    return k*np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**2

def beta_p(t,k=3.0):
    return k*np.cos(t)*(1-3*np.sin(t)**2)

def beta_pp(t,k=3.0):
    return k*(-7*np.sin(t)+9*np.sin(t)**3)

for k in [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 3.8, 4.0]:
    ts=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,200001)
    b=beta_fn(ts,k)
    print("k",k,"max|beta|",np.max(np.abs(b)), "deg",np.degrees(np.max(np.abs(b))))

import numpy as np, math
from scipy.integrate import quad

def beta(t,k):
    return k*np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**2

def betap(t,k):
    return k*np.cos(t)*(1-3*np.sin(t)**2)

def speed(t,k):
    b=beta(t,k)
    return np.sqrt(betap(t,k)**2 + 4*np.cos(b)**2)

for k in [0,0.1,0.5,1,2,3,3.8,4.0]:
    L=quad(lambda x:speed(x,k),0,2*np.pi,epsabs=1e-12,epsrel=1e-12)[0]
    print(k,L,L/(2*np.pi),np.degrees(2*k/(3*np.sqrt(3))))

import numpy as np, math
from scipy.integrate import quad
from scipy.optimize import brentq

def f_shape(t,q):
    return np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**2*(1+q*np.sin(2*t)**2)

def f1_shape(t,q):
    # numerical? analytic derivative with product
    s=np.sin(t); c=np.cos(t); u=np.sin(2*t)
    return c*(1-3*s*s)*(1+q*u*u) + s*c*c*q*4*u*np.cos(2*t)

def lobe_len(k,q):
    def sp(t):
        b=k*f_shape(t,q)
        bp=k*f1_shape(t,q)
        return np.sqrt(bp*bp+4*np.cos(b)**2)
    return quad(sp,0,np.pi,epsabs=1e-10,epsrel=1e-10,limit=200)[0]

def kcrit_q(q):
    ts=np.linspace(0,np.pi,200001)
    fm=np.max(f_shape(ts,q))
    return np.pi/(2*fm)

for q in [0,0.25,0.5,1,2,3,5,10]:
    kc=kcrit_q(q)
    ll0=lobe_len(0.00001,q)
    llmax=lobe_len(kc*(1-1e-5),q)
    print("q",q,"kcrit",kc,"lobe min",ll0,"max",llmax,"max/pi",llmax/np.pi)

import numpy as np, math
from scipy.integrate import quad
from scipy.optimize import brentq, minimize_scalar

def shape_beta(t,a,c):
    return a*np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**2 + c*np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**4
def shape_b1(t,a,c):
    s=np.sin(t); co=np.cos(t)
    return a*(co**3-2*s**2*co) + c*(co**5-4*s**2*co**3)
def shape_b2(t,a,c):
    s=np.sin(t); co=np.cos(t)
    # differentiate terms:
    # d(co^3 -2s²co) = -3co²s -4s co² +2s³ = 2s³ -7s co²
    # d(co^5 -4s²co³)= -5s co^4 -8s co^4 +12s³ co² = 12s³co² -13s co^4
    return a*(2*s**3-7*s*co**2) + c*(12*s**3*co**2-13*s*co**4)

def speed(t,a,c):
    bb=shape_beta(t,a,c)
    return math.sqrt(shape_b1(t,a,c)**2 + 4*math.cos(bb)**2)

def kg(t,a,c):
    bb=shape_beta(t,a,c); b1=shape_b1(t,a,c); b2=shape_b2(t,a,c)
    spd=speed(t,a,c)
    det=2*(2*math.sin(bb)*b1*b1 + math.sin(bb)+math.sin(3*bb)+math.cos(bb)*b2)
    return det/spd**3

def area_lobe_ac(a,c):
    return 2*quad(lambda x: 1-math.sin(shape_beta(x,a,c)),0,math.pi,epsabs=1e-11)[0]

def find_a(c):
    # area lobe = pi; search a positive. c is dimensionless; need a+c cos² >=0
    # lower bound a > max(0,-c)
    lo=max(0,-c)+1e-8
    hi=20
    f=lambda a: area_lobe_ac(a,c)-math.pi
    # ensure no β > pi/2 maybe constrain max beta
    # increase high until area below pi, but avoid nonmonotonic beyond hemisphere
    grid=np.linspace(lo,hi,500)
    vals=[]
    prev=(grid[0],f(grid[0]))
    for x in grid[1:]:
        fx=f(x)
        if prev[1]*fx<=0:
            return brentq(f,prev[0],x,xtol=1e-12)
        prev=(x,fx)
    return None

def smooth_energy(c):
    a=find_a(c)
    if a is None: return np.inf
    # Check beta max under pi/2
    vals=np.linspace(0,math.pi,2001)
    betas=np.array([shape_beta(x,a,c) for x in vals])
    if np.max(betas)>=math.pi/2: return np.inf
    # kg derivative numerical complex? use central finite diff at high N for quick objective
    N=3000
    ts=np.linspace(0,math.pi,N+1)
    kgs=np.array([kg(x,a,c) for x in ts])
    # periodic endpoints? lobe branch t 0 to pi has crossing E different tangent. k_g at t0 vs tpi maybe sign? For full curve curvature continuity across seam at t=pi to next lobe? This parameterization changes sign etc. But objective on full 2pi.
    # derivative np.gradient with second-order edge; integrate on lobe, both branches. use periodic full 2pi instead.
    ts=np.linspace(0,2*math.pi,2*N+1)
    kgs=np.array([kg(x,a,c) for x in ts])
    # derivative wrt t central periodic
    dt=ts[1]-ts[0]
    kgp=(np.roll(kgs,-1)-np.roll(kgs,1))/(2*dt)
    spds=np.array([speed(x,a,c) for x in ts])
    # full curve J = int kgp^2 / speed dt
    return np.trapz(kgp**2/spds,ts)

for c0 in [-1,-.5,0,.5,1,1.5,2]:
    a0=find_a(c0)
    print(c0,a0,smooth_energy(c0))

## [1126] ASSISTANT · 2026-11-02T06:14:57.309Z

That gives us a much better design constraint. The Analemma's shape can be determined by **area balance**, rather than arbitrarily choosing how broad or narrow its lobes should be. Then its total length determines the torus gearing.

I have worked through a candidate construction numerically.

## 1. Equal-area Analemma

I'll interpret *inner area* as the combined areas of the northern and southern lobes, and *outer area* as the remaining equatorial region of the sphere.

The desired condition is:

\[
A_{\text{north}}+A_{\text{south}}
=A_{\text{equatorial remainder}}
=2\pi b^2
\]

where \(b\) is the sphere radius.

A useful spherical construction is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi(t)&=2t\\
\beta(t)&=k\sin t\cos^2t\\
G(t)&=b
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\beta(t)\cos\phi(t)\\
\cos\beta(t)\sin\phi(t)\\
\sin\beta(t)
\end{pmatrix}
\end{aligned}
\qquad 0\leq t\leq2\pi
\]

This gives us:

- Northern lobe around the north pole, \(0<t<\pi\).
- Southern lobe around the south pole, \(\pi<t<2\pi\).
- Transverse crossing at east, \(E=(b,0,0)\).
- Tangential kissing point at west, \(W=(-b,0,0)\).

The branches cross at E with distinct tangent directions. At W they share a tangent line but have opposite transverse curvature. Both conditions are built into the geometry.

<badge color="success">Numerically solved</badge> **The equal-area condition gives**

\[
\boxed{k=2.6349970963}
\]

The maximum latitude of either lobe is approximately \(58.11^\circ\).

Each lobe encloses exactly one quarter of the sphere's total surface area. Together, they occupy half the sphere, leaving the other half in the equatorial region.

## 2. Total Analemma length

The spherical arc-length integral is

\[
L_A=2b\int_0^\pi
\sqrt{
\left(\frac{d\beta}{dt}\right)^2+
4\cos^2\beta
}\,dt
\]

Numerical integration gives:

\[
\boxed{L_A=13.2691350396\,b}
\]

This is a useful result. The topology itself imposes a lower bound of \(4\pi b\), because each lobe must connect two antipodal points by two arcs. Our equal-area construction exceeds that minimum by approximately 5.59%.

## 3. The torus gearing

Your latest instruction establishes the gearing condition:

\[
2\pi(R-b)=2nL_A
\]

where \(n\) is a positive integer. Thus the inner torus circumference contains an even number of complete Analemma circuits.

For the smallest possible even multiple, \(n=1\):

\[
\boxed{\frac{R}{b}=5.2236968642}
\]

Higher even multiples produce:

| Analemma circuits per inner circumference | Required \(R/b\) |
|---:|---:|
| 2 | 5.2237 |
| 4 | 9.4474 |
| 6 | 13.6711 |
| 8 | 17.8948 |

<text color="secondary" size="xs">These are calculated ratios for the equal-area candidate, not arbitrary preset values.</text>

### What this means for the current instrument

The current browser defaults are \(R=1.65\) and \(b=0.55\), giving \(R/b=3\). Their inner circumference is only about 94.7% of one complete equal-area Analemma.

For the minimum two-circuit gearing, we have two choices:

- Preserve \(b=0.55\): increase the major radius to \(R=2.87303\).
- Preserve \(R=1.65\): reduce the sphere and tube radius to \(b=0.31587\).

The existing dimensions cannot satisfy the new geometry and gearing simultaneously.

## 4. One further refinement: actual rotational smoothness

There is an important distinction between equal-area balance and minimum rotational acceleration.

In the current inner-wall rolling model, the sphere's radial angular-velocity component is proportional to the Analemma's signed geodesic curvature, \(\kappa_g\). Consequently, the way that curvature changes along the Analemma directly affects the smoothness of the rotation.

I recommend treating equal area as a hard geometric constraint, then optimizing the shape against a rotational smoothness functional:

\[
J_{\mathrm{rot}}=
\int_0^{2\pi}
\left\|
\frac{d}{d\psi}
\left(\frac{\boldsymbol{\omega}}{\dot\psi}\right)
\right\|^2d\psi
\]

That gives us an actual mathematical target rather than assuming equal areas automatically minimize acceleration. We can explore a richer family of curves, preserve the crossing, kissing, pole and area conditions, and numerically minimize this quantity.

## [1136] ASSISTANT · 2026-11-02T06:25:55.256Z

Then the dimensions are determined by the geometry, with one remaining freedom: **overall scale**.

I'll preserve the existing tube and sphere radius, \(b=a=0.55\). Their circumferences therefore remain identical:

\[
C_{\rm sphere}=C_{\rm tube}=2\pi(0.55)
\]

The equal-area Analemma has length \(L_A=13.2691350396b\). For the minimum even gearing, two complete Analemma circuits per inner torus circumference:

\[
2\pi(R-b)=2L_A
\]

This sets the major radius to:

\[
\boxed{R=2.8730332753}
\]

So the sphere does not need to shrink, the tube does not need to grow, and the required ratio is achieved by enlarging the torus's major radius. The next step is to make the browser model enforce this relationship rather than letting its old independent radius controls silently violate it.

The Whirligig-specific rebuild is now committed to `main`:

- R and Q now encircle the north and south poles, respectively.
- The Analemma now has its E crossing and W tangency, with equal-area lobes.
- The major radius is derived from the sphere/tube radius. The independent major-radius slider is gone, so the gear ratio cannot be broken accidentally.
- The sphere and tube circumferences remain equal. The scale control expands or contracts both together.
- I reduced the R/Q aperture gain to keep the crossbar midpoint near the sphere center.

The scripted regression covered **117,684 geometry samples** across 84 configurations. It found no missing torus-wall hits, no hemisphere violations, and residuals around \(10^{-12}\) to \(10^{-15}\) for the meridian, perpendicularity, and selected-contact constraints. The default W_obble midpoint offset is \(0.093b\).

The repository change is on `main`, commit [`04a2cbb`](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/commit/04a2cbbdae426e70973872ad13b5bf0ee0b639fc). Only four Whirligig-specific files changed. The site-wide deployment workflow and unrelated routes were left untouched.

**Two limitations remain:**

1. The Curvy Lisa output still exhibits first-hit branch jumps, reaching about 2.75 model units in the full test matrix. These are reported, not smoothed away. Adaptive root continuation remains necessary.
2. Equal-area balance is now satisfied, but it is not yet proven to minimize rotational acceleration. That requires a separate constrained optimization of the Analemma's curvature evolution.

<badge color="warning">Deployment not yet verified</badge>

The existing GitHub Pages deployment workflow has started, but its run is still in progress at checkout. Its Whirligig-specific build and deployment steps have not completed, so I am not claiming the updated instrument is live.

import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import quad
from scipy.optimize import brentq

PI = np.pi
TWO_PI = 2*PI

def beta(t, k):
    return k*np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**2

def beta_p(t, k):
    s, c = np.sin(t), np.cos(t)
    return k*c*(1-3*s*s)

def beta_pp(t, k):
    s = np.sin(t)
    return k*s*(9*s*s-7)

def lobe_area(k):
    return 2*quad(lambda t: 1-np.sin(beta(t,k)), 0, PI,
                  epsabs=1e-13, epsrel=1e-13)[0]

k = brentq(lambda x: lobe_area(x)-PI, 2.5, 3.0, xtol=1e-14)
L_unit = quad(lambda t: np.sqrt(beta_p(t,k)**2 + 4*np.cos(beta(t,k))**2),
              0, TWO_PI, epsabs=1e-13, epsrel=1e-13)[0]
gear_ratio = 1 + L_unit/PI
b = 0.55
R = gear_ratio*b
L_physical = L_unit*b
sphere_tube_circ = TWO_PI*b
inner_torus_circ = TWO_PI*(R-b)

# Maximum latitude by a dense scan.
ts = np.linspace(0, PI, 1_000_001)
max_lat = float(np.max(beta(ts,k)))

# Exact branch tangents at crossing E (t=0, pi) and kissing W (pi/2, 3pi/2)
# in local (e_phi, e_beta) components.
tE0 = np.array([2.0, k])
tE1 = np.array([2.0, -k])
crossing_det = float(np.linalg.det(np.stack([tE0,tE1])))
tW0 = np.array([2.0, 0.0])
tW1 = np.array([2.0, 0.0])

# Numerical check of the analytic first/second derivatives.
def G(t):
    be=beta(t,k)
    return np.array([np.cos(be)*np.cos(2*t),
                     np.cos(be)*np.sin(2*t),
                     np.sin(be)])

def G1(t):
    be,bp=beta(t,k),beta_p(t,k)
    eb=np.array([-np.sin(be)*np.cos(2*t),-np.sin(be)*np.sin(2*t),np.cos(be)])
    ep=np.array([-np.sin(2*t),np.cos(2*t),0.0])
    return bp*eb+2*np.cos(be)*ep

def G2(t):
    be,bp,bpp=beta(t,k),beta_p(t,k),beta_pp(t,k)
    g=G(t)
    eb=np.array([-np.sin(be)*np.cos(2*t),-np.sin(be)*np.sin(2*t),np.cos(be)])
    ep=np.array([-np.sin(2*t),np.cos(2*t),0.0])
    return (bpp+4*np.sin(be)*np.cos(be))*eb - 4*bp*np.sin(be)*ep - (bp*bp+4*np.cos(be)**2)*g

hs=[1e-3,5e-4,2.5e-4]
deriv_errors=[]
for h in hs:
    t=.713
    fd1=(G(t+h)-G(t-h))/(2*h)
    fd2=(G(t+h)-2*G(t)+G(t-h))/(h*h)
    deriv_errors.append((h,float(np.linalg.norm(fd1-G1(t))),float(np.linalg.norm(fd2-G2(t)))))

# Verify full circuit and two-circuit gearing.
delta = gear_ratio-1
assert abs(TWO_PI*delta - 2*L_unit) < 1e-12
assert abs(sphere_tube_circ - TWO_PI*b) < 1e-14
assert abs(inner_torus_circ - 2*L_physical) < 1e-12
assert abs(lobe_area(k)-PI) < 1e-12
assert abs(2*lobe_area(k) - (4*PI - 2*lobe_area(k))) < 1e-12

{
    "k": k,
    "one_lobe_area": lobe_area(k),
    "two_lobe_area": 2*lobe_area(k),
    "equatorial_remainder_area": 4*PI-2*lobe_area(k),
    "max_latitude_degrees": np.degrees(max_lat),
    "unit_sphere_analemma_length": L_unit,
    "gear_ratio_R_over_b": gear_ratio,
    "b": b,

    "sphere_and_tube_circumference": sphere_tube_circ,
    "inner_torus_circumference": inner_torus_circ,
    "inner_circumference_over_analemma_length": inner_torus_circ/L_physical,
    "crossing_tangent_determinant": crossing_det,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent validation of the Whirligig equal-area spherical Analemma."""
from __future__ import annotations
import math

PI = math.pi
TAU = 2.0 * PI


def simpson(f, a: float, b: float, n: int = 8192) -> float:
    if n % 2:
        raise ValueError("Simpson interval count must be even")
    h = (b - a) / n
    total = f(a) + f(b)
    total += 4.0 * sum(f(a + (2*i - 1)*h) for i in range(1, n//2 + 1))
    total += 2.0 * sum(f(a + 2*i*h) for i in range(1, n//2))
    return total * h / 3.0


def beta(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    return k * math.sin(t) * math.cos(t)**2


def beta_p(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    s, c = math.sin(t), math.cos(t)
    return k * c * (1.0 - 3.0*s*s)


def beta_pp(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    s = math.sin(t)
    return k * s * (9.0*s*s - 7.0)


def lobe_area(k: float) -> float:
    # d(longitude)/dt = 2; north-polar lobe area = integral(1-sin(latitude)) d(longitude).
    return 2.0 * simpson(lambda t: 1.0 - math.sin(beta(t, k)), 0.0, PI)


def unit_analemma(t: float, k: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    be = beta(t, k)
    return (math.cos(be)*math.cos(2*t),
            math.cos(be)*math.sin(2*t),
            math.sin(be))


def unit_analemma_d1(t: float, k: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    be, bp = beta(t, k), beta_p(t, k)
    cb, sb, cp, sp = math.cos(be), math.sin(be), math.cos(2*t), math.sin(2*t)
    return (-bp*sb*cp - 2*cb*sp,
            -bp*sb*sp + 2*cb*cp,
            bp*cb)


def unit_analemma_d2(t: float, k: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    be, bp, bpp = beta(t, k), beta_p(t, k), beta_pp(t, k)
    cb, sb, cp, sp = math.cos(be), math.sin(be), math.cos(2*t), math.sin(2*t)
    e_beta = (-sb*cp, -sb*sp, cb)
    e_phi = (-sp, cp, 0.0)
    g = unit_analemma(t, k)
    a = bpp + 4.0*sb*cb
    d = -4.0*bp*sb
    q = -(bp*bp + 4.0*cb*cb)
    return tuple(a*e_beta[i] + d*e_phi[i] + q*g[i] for i in range(3))


def dot(a, b):
    return sum(x*y for x, y in zip(a, b))


def cross(a, b):
    return (a[1]*b[2]-a[2]*b[1],
            a[2]*b[0]-a[0]*b[2],
            a[0]*b[1]-a[1]*b[0])


def norm(a):
    return math.sqrt(dot(a, a))


def analemma_speed(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    be, bp = beta(t, k), beta_p(t, k)
    return math.hypot(bp, 2.0*math.cos(be))


def analemma_length(k: float) -> float:
    return simpson(lambda t: analemma_speed(t, k), 0.0, TAU)


def solve_k() -> float:
    lo, hi = 2.5, 3.0
    flo = lobe_area(lo) - PI
    fhi = lobe_area(hi) - PI
    if flo * fhi >= 0:
        raise RuntimeError("Equal-area root is not bracketed")
    for _ in range(80):
        mid = 0.5*(lo+hi)
        fm = lobe_area(mid) - PI
        if flo*fm <= 0:
            hi, fhi = mid, fm
        else:
            lo, flo = mid, fm
    return 0.5*(lo+hi)


def main() -> None:
    k = solve_k()
    area_each = lobe_area(k)
    area_two = 2.0*area_each
    area_remainder = 4.0*PI-area_two
    length_unit = analemma_length(k)
    even_circuits = 2
    ratio = 1.0 + even_circuits*length_unit/TAU
    b = 0.55  # retain the existing tube/sphere radius; absolute scale is free
    R = ratio*b
    length_physical = length_unit*b
    sphere_circ = TAU*b
    tube_circ = TAU*b
    inner_torus_circ = TAU*(R-b)

    # Exact local branch conditions: E is transverse; W is tangential.
    e_branch_1 = (2.0, k)    # (e_phi, e_beta) at t=0
    e_branch_2 = (2.0, -k)   # (e_phi, e_beta) at t=pi
    e_det = e_branch_1[0]*e_branch_2[1] - e_branch_1[1]*e_branch_2[0]
    w_branch_1 = (2.0, 0.0)  # at t=pi/2
    w_branch_2 = (2.0, 0.0)  # at t=3pi/2
    w_tangent_dot = dot(w_branch_1, w_branch_2)/(norm(w_branch_1)*norm(w_branch_2))

    # Check the analytic first and second derivatives against central differences.
    derivative_errors = []
    t0 = 0.713
    for h in (1e-3, 5e-4, 2.5e-4):
        gm, g0, gp = unit_analemma(t0-h,k), unit_analemma(t0,k), unit_analemma(t0+h,k)
        fd1 = tuple((gp[i]-gm[i])/(2*h) for i in range(3))
        fd2 = tuple((gp[i]-2*g0[i]+gm[i])/(h*h) for i in range(3))
        derivative_errors.append((h, norm(tuple(fd1[i]-unit_analemma_d1(t0,k)[i] for i in range(3))),
                                  norm(tuple(fd2[i]-unit_analemma_d2(t0,k)[i] for i in range(3)))))

    # Curvature and speed remain finite and regular over one material circuit.
    min_speed = float("inf")
    max_abs_kg = 0.0
    for i in range(8192):
        t = TAU*i/8192
        g, v1, v2 = unit_analemma(t,k), unit_analemma_d1(t,k), unit_analemma_d2(t,k)
        speed = norm(v1)
        kg = dot(g, cross(v1,v2))/(speed**3)
        min_speed = min(min_speed, speed)
        max_abs_kg = max(max_abs_kg, abs(kg))

    # The latitude maximum occurs at sin^2(t)=1/3.
    max_lat = 2.0*k/(3.0*math.sqrt(3.0))

    assert abs(area_each-PI) < 2e-11
    assert abs(area_two-area_remainder) < 2e-11
    assert abs(e_det) > 1e-8
    assert abs(w_tangent_dot-1.0) < 1e-14
    assert min_speed > 1.0
    assert abs(TAU*(ratio-1.0)-even_circuits*length_unit) < 2e-11
    assert abs(inner_torus_circ-even_circuits*length_physical) < 2e-11
    assert abs(sphere_circ-tube_circ) < 1e-14

    print(f"area-balance shape k                 = {k:.13f}")
    print(f"one lobe area                       = {area_each:.13f} b^2 sr")
    print(f"both lobes area                     = {area_two:.13f} b^2 sr")
    print(f"equatorial remainder area           = {area_remainder:.13f} b^2 sr")
    print(f"maximum lobe latitude               = {math.degrees(max_lat):.9f} deg")
    print(f"full Analemma length / b            = {length_unit:.13f}")
    print(f"minimum even circuit count          = {even_circuits}")
    print(f"required major/minor ratio R/b      = {ratio:.13f}")
    print(f"chosen tube/sphere radius b         = {b:.8f}")
    print(f"derived torus major radius R        = {R:.13f}")
    print(f"physical Analemma length            = {length_physical:.13f}")
    print(f"sphere great-circle circumference   = {sphere_circ:.13f}")
    print(f"tube cross-section circumference    = {tube_circ:.13f}")
    print(f"inner torus circumference           = {inner_torus_circ:.13f}")
    print(f"inner circumference / Analemma L   = {inner_torus_circ/length_physical:.13f}")
    print(f"E crossing tangent determinant      = {e_det:.13f} (nonzero = transverse)")
    print(f"W kissing tangent dot               = {w_tangent_dot:.13f} (1 = common tangent)")
    print(f"minimum spherical parameter speed   = {min_speed:.13f}")
    print(f"maximum |geodesic curvature|        = {max_abs_kg:.13f}")
    print("derivative finite-difference checks:")
    for h, e1, e2 in derivative_errors:
        print(f"  h={h:.7g}: first={e1:.3e}, second={e2:.3e}")
    print("PASS: equal areas, topology, regularity, radius equality, and 2:1 inner-circumference gearing")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The area-balance parameter is numerically solved, and the full material length sets the minimum even gearing: two complete Analemma circuits per inner-torus circumference. The major radius is derived from that ratio; the tube/sphere radius is the overall scale control. The selected contact obeys the analytic no-slip condition at one nominated point only; because equal radii create a nonisolated contact set, this does <b>not</b> certify no-slip across every point of contact. There is no separate pen or projector. The only tracing member is the single gimbal elbow, constrained perpendicular to the moving crossbar. The inner contact is Donomphulon; P_ivot is the separate outer radial point, with BigRad joining the radial construction. The R/Q equation-to-sphere mapping is an explicit representation choice, not a derived physical law. Equal area is a geometric balance condition, not yet a proof of globally minimum angular acceleration. Legacy GrAnn identifiers are implementation history only; the user-facing component is Analemma. This is not a certified physical bearing model and does not establish equation isomorphism.
